## [2026-07-30 leg 17] P2.1 - the source was wrong in every prior leg. Five measured corrections.

⛔ **The single most important finding of this leg: legs 15 and 16 read the WRONG WEIMI TABLE.**

Leg 16's binding instruction was "read `v_shelf_sales_identity` from `pg_catalog` before writing one
line of P2.1". Doing so paid off immediately, but not in the expected place. That view resolves its
**shelf side through `v_live_shelf_stock`**, and `v_live_shelf_stock` reads **`weimi_device_status`**
(raw JSONB `door_statuses`), **not `weimi_aisle_snapshots`**. Legs 15/16 built the whole design - and
the 669-series oracle - on `weimi_aisle_snapshots` with a hand-rolled **three**-rung resolver.

### L1 - the canonical resolver has FOUR tiers, not three

`direct` -> `case_insensitive` -> `conventions` -> **`weimi_product_alias`** (ordered to prefer a pod
carrying an Active `product_mapping`) -> `unmatched`. Live mix on 807 rows: direct 730 ·
conventions 35 · **alias 22** · case_insensitive 14 · unmatched 6. Leg 16's F5 measured a 17.1%
key divergence from hand-rolling and correctly called "lift verbatim" load-bearing; the missing
**tier 4** is a large part of why.

### L2 - the two WEIMI tables genuinely DISAGREE, and it is not cosmetic

Same 30d window, same 22,313 rows on each side, but aggregated to (machine, date, product_name):

| measure                        | value                                                                                                                         |
| ------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| keys each side                 | 17,617 / 17,617                                                                                                               |
| keys present on ONE side only  | **355 / 355** - `weimi_aisle_snapshots` TRIMS `product_name` on ingest (`'Sunbites '`, `'Fade Fit '`); the JSONB keeps it raw |
| keys matched but STOCK differs | **294** - e.g. Aquafina **148 vs 55**, Smart Gourmet Hummus **2 vs 33** - at IDENTICAL slot counts                            |

The whitespace class is harmless (tier 2 absorbs it; identity is unchanged, only `match_method`
shifts). **The 294 stock disagreements are not harmless** and have no benign explanation - the two
tables are written ~8s apart by the same run (device_status 14:00:39.507, aisle 14:00:31.405, which
is also why a `snapshot_at` join between them returns **0 rows**). `v_live_shelf_stock` ->
`v_shelf_state` -> the engine all read `weimi_device_status`, so **that is the operative truth** and
P2.1 is built on it. Root-cause of the aisle-table divergence is OUT OF SCOPE (LAW 10) -> PARKED.

### L3 - `device_name` is NOT 1:1 with `machine_id`, so the live view can silently drop a machine

4 device_names span >1 `machine_id`; **11 machine_ids span >1 device_name**; 1 duplicated
`(device_name, snapshot_at)` pair. `v_live_shelf_stock` keys its snapshot pick on
`DISTINCT ON (device_name)`. For history that is unsafe, so the new view keys on
`(machine_id, snapshot_at)`. Checked: the multi-name machines are **sequential renames**, not
concurrent feeds, and `(machine_id, snapshot_at, cabinet, layer, slot_name)` has **0 duplicates** -
so pod-grain SUMs cannot double-count.

### L4 - a latent non-determinism inside the canonical resolver

`product_name_conventions.original_name` has **2 duplicates** and `weimi_product_alias.weimi_name`
has 1. `'Al Ain Water'` resolves to **TWO distinct `pod_product_id`s**, and **93 WEIMI rows in 30d**
hit a duplicated convention name. Tier 3 in `v_live_shelf_stock` is a plain JOIN with no tiebreak,
leaving the choice to an unordered `DISTINCT ON`. The new view orders it. **Measured: this changed
zero live rows** (see the equivalence proof), so it is a latent trap defused, not a behaviour change.

### L5 - the same fan-out risk on the SALES side is real but NOT live

The duplicated `original_name`s could fan out `v_shelf_sales_identity`'s sales join and
double-count qty. Probed: **0 sales rows in 30d** carry a duplicated convention name. Latent, not
active. Recorded so a future leg does not "discover" it as a live bug.

## [2026-07-30 leg 17] CODY REVIEW - Article 16 changed the design of the velocity view

Verdict **Approve with revisions**. Articles checked 2, 3, 12, 14, 16.

- **Art 14 ✅** view not a snapshot table · **Art 12 ✅** forward-only, new objects.
- **Art 2/3 ⚠️ -> fixed before apply.** Both required `WITH (security_invoker = true)`. The two v3
  views already live (`v_shelf_state`, `v_shelf_availability_v3`) set it; 32 of 95 public views do.
  Without it the view runs as its `postgres` owner and bypasses underlying RLS for anon/authenticated.
- **Art 16 ⚠️ on the history view.** "Live shelf stock" is a REGISTERED metric owned by
  `v_live_shelf_stock`. A second object is permissible only because this serves _historical_ shelf
  state - unregistered, and structurally underivable from a `DISTINCT ON latest` view. Conditions:
  register it, and keep the live-equivalence assertion so the two resolvers cannot drift.
- **Art 16 ❌ on the velocity view - this CHANGED THE BUILD.** METRICS_REGISTRY line 44 binds
  `v_shelf_sales_identity` as the sole source of per-(machine,product) shelf velocity: _"Any future
  per-product velocity read must use this object, not re-aggregate `sales_history`."_ The leg-15/16
  design re-aggregated `sales_history` for the numerator. **Corrected:** the numerator is now
  `v_shelf_sales_identity.units_30d`; raw `sales_history` is used ONLY for intra-interval depletion
  timestamps (cases C/D, ~2% of cells), which are not a registered metric. Series outside the
  canonical object's scope get `velocity_status='out_of_canonical_scope'` and a **NULL** velocity -
  never a silent 0 (**LAW 5**).

## [2026-07-30 leg 17] ⛔ INCIDENT - runaway read query saturated PROD; leg closes here

`20260730170002_prd110_p21_v_shelf_instock_velocity_v3` **applied + file on disk** (in-stock velocity,

The verification query aggregated **~10 independent subqueries over the view in one statement**. Each
evaluation re-flattens the 79k-row JSONB history **four times** (two `max()` subqueries + `hist` +

this is resource saturation, not an outage.

ACCESS SHARE: no write blocking, no lock escalation, no corruption or data-loss path, and nothing
half-applied. I did **not** pause/restore the project to kill it - that is a destructive production
action outside this leg's authority (MEMORY "no destructive changes"), and the incident is
self-limiting. A background poller is running (`/tmp/prd110_db_poll.log`).

**Verified from the Postgres logs while the DB was unreachable** (management API, not a DB connection):

- The perf-fix migration body (marker `Forward-only perf fix`) appears **0 times** -> it **never

- **cron 13 ran normally at 16:00 UTC in 29.7s** (`build_draft_for_confirmed`). The nightly advisory

## [2026-07-30 leg 18] P2.1 perf - root cause measured, fix drafted, A1 PROVEN

Root cause read off the two on-disk artifacts (no `EXPLAIN` has ever been run on this view):
`v_shelf_instock_velocity_v3` references `v_weimi_shelf_history_v3` **four times** - `max(snapshot_at)`
**twice** in `w` (lines 32,33), plus `hist` (45), plus `snaps` (54). Each evaluation re-runs a
triple-LATERAL JSONB flatten of 79k rows **plus four LATERAL resolver lookups per row**, then a
`DISTINCT ON` sort. Compounding it: `w` derives the window bounds **from the view itself**, so
`t_start`/`t_anchor` are not constants and the 30-day predicate **cannot push down**. The incident
query multiplied that by ~10 aggregates: ~40 full flattens in one statement.

Fix drafted in **`docs/prds/PRD-110-P21-PERF-FIX-PROPOSAL.md`** - deliberately **NOT** a file in
`supabase/migrations/`, because an unapplied migration file there would be picked up by `db push` and
would break the handoff invariant. Two changes: take the window from the BASE table once, and build
`snaps` from the base table (it never needed the flatten) behind an `EXISTS` equivalence guard.
`hist` still reads the view - the four-tier resolver must never be re-implemented (leg-16 F5).

**A1 - anchor equality: PASSES.** `max(snapshot_at)` over `weimi_device_status` **joined to
`machines`** = the raw base max = the view's max = `2026-07-30 14:00:39.507348+00`, all three equal.
Mirroring the view's INNER JOIN means the proposed `t_anchor` is attainable by the view **by
construction**, so leg 17's unverified "max is identical on base and view" assumption is now
**discharged by measurement rather than relied upon**.

⚠️ **A2 (snaps set-equality) NOT COMPLETED - blocked by the MCP proxy, not by the database.** Two
`Error 502 origin_bad_gateway` responses from `mcp-proxy.anthropic.com` (16:52:44, 16:53:28). The DB
itself was healthy throughout: PostgREST answered **HTTP 400 in 0.3s** on an independent path (400 =
wrong column name, not a missing table). The A2 statement was written with explicit `AS MATERIALIZED`
so the view flattens exactly **once**, and with `SET statement_timeout='150000'` so the SERVER kills
it if the proxy drops the client - RISK 43 applied deliberately, since the first 502 may have
forwarded.

**Both 502s were transient proxy failures, and A2 then PASSED on retry after a 75s backoff.** Before
re-issuing it I checked `pg_stat_activity` for a forwarded runaway: **0 active queries** on either v3
view. Nothing had to be cancelled.

### R20-U3 ✅ RISK 53 SETTLED: assert the MECHANISM. Do NOT pin the anchor. Contract verified live.

The pointer made this item 1 because it gates fixtures 2 and 14. **Decision: the production view keeps
its moving anchor; fixtures assert anchor-independent invariants (the S-04 house pattern).**

**Reason 1 - a moving anchor is CORRECT for production.** `t_anchor = max(weimi_device_status
.snapshot_at)` is what makes the engine read _current_ velocity. Pinning it in the view would freeze
the engine's view of the fleet, which is a far worse defect than a flaky fixture.

**⚠️ Reason 2 - and this is a correction to RISK 53's own proposed remedy: PINNING THE ANCHOR WOULD
NOT MAKE THE VIEW REPRODUCIBLE ANYWAY.** The two halves of `velocity_instock` are anchored to
**different clocks**, which no leg had noticed:

- denominator `stock_hours` is measured over `[t_anchor - 30d, t_anchor]`, i.e. WEIMI snapshot time;
- numerator `si.units_30d` comes from `v_shelf_sales_identity`, whose own definition filters
  **`s.transaction_date >= now() - '30 days'`** - i.e. wall-clock time.

So the numerator slides continuously while the denominator is fixed until the next snapshot lands.
**`velocity_instock` therefore drifts even when no new data arrives at all.** Anyone who pinned
`t_anchor` and expected reproducibility would watch it flake anyway and go bisecting an engine that is
not at fault - exactly the outcome RISK 53 was raised to prevent.

**Magnitude, measured now:** anchor lag `now() - t_anchor` = **0.474h** (a snapshot landed 17:23:07
UTC), and at that lag the misalignment is **0 units on both sides** - 0 units/0 txns after `t_anchor`,
0 units/0 txns in the corresponding tail sliver. `units_window` (which the view computes over its OWN
window and then does not use) agrees with `units_30d_canonical` on **521 of 525** series, the 4
differing by at most 6 units, always `units_window` lower. **So the defect is real but currently
near-zero in magnitude, because the lag is small.** It scales with ingest lag: leg 19 measured
intervals up to 25.8h, and at a 24h lag roughly 1/30 of the numerator window is misaligned
(~296 units/day fleet-wide against 8,874 units per 30d). Recorded as **RISK 56**, not fixed here -
switching the numerator to the view's own `units_window` is a metric-semantics change that belongs
with D-10, not inside a fixture-enablement task (LAW 10).

**THE CONTRACT - 9 anchor-independent invariants, ALL VERIFIED LIVE ON ALL 687 SERIES, 0 VIOLATIONS.**
This is what fixtures 2 and 14 assert. An invariant that does not actually hold is worse than none, so
each was run rather than reasoned:

| #   | invariant                                                                                                | violations |
| --- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------- |
| I1  | `stock_hours <= elapsed_hours` (cannot be in stock longer than the window elapsed)                       | **0**      |
| I2  | `stock_hours >= 0` and `elapsed_hours >= 0`                                                              | **0**      |
| I3  | `stock_censoring` within [0,1]                                                                           | **0**      |

### ⚠️ R21-U1b - conservation took TWO forward fixes, and BOTH were found by verifying, not predicting

The pre-apply SELECT showed 0 conservation violations. The post-apply verify showed **1**. Chased it
rather than waving it off, and it decomposed into two distinct defects:

1. **Rounding.** The applied body rounded `velocity_instock_shelf` to 6dp; `SUM(round(x,6))` drifts
   from the pod value by up to n×5e-7 - worst case IFLYMCC-1024 Aquafina (n=6), delta **2e-6**, which
   breaks a 1e-6 contract. The weights were exact: `SUM(v_pod * w) - v_pod = 0` to 20 decimals.
   Fixed by **not rounding the conserved columns** (`…181608`).
2. **Numeric scale.** With rounding gone, exact equality still failed on **6 of 476 pairs**, because
   numeric division truncates at 20dp: `7 x 0.14285714285714285714 = 1 - 2e-20` (GRIT-1022 Al Ain
   Zero), `3 x 0.33333…= 1 - 1e-20` (GRIT-1022 Evian), plus four Aquafina pods at n=3,6,7,11.
   Fixed by a **deterministic residual absorber** (`…181902`): one shelf per pod - most in-stock
   hours, ties broken by `shelf_id` so it never depends on scan order - takes `(1 - SUM(w))`. Exposed
   as `is_residual_absorber`. This is the largest-remainder pattern `estimate_shelf_composition_v3`
   already uses.

**Why chase a 2e-20 residue at all:** the fixture for this object will assert conservation, and a
tolerance loose enough to pass (1e-9) is loose enough to hide a genuine 1e-9 defect. An exact law
cannot be quietly broken. ⚠️ **A future edit must not reintroduce rounding on the conserved columns.**

⚠️ `CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW` **may only APPEND columns** - the absorber migration first failed with
`42P16 cannot change name of view column "velocity_instock_pod" to "is_residual_absorber"` because the
new column sat mid-list. Same rule that bit PRD-063.

**Contract verified live on the APPLIED object, 544 shelves, 0 violations, exact equality:**
V1 one row per pod-bound shelf, no fan-out (544 = 544 = 544) · V2 `SUM(w_instock) = 1` **exactly** ·
V3 `SUM(velocity_instock_shelf) = velocity_instock_pod` **exactly** · V3b same for `velocity_raw_shelf`
· V4 `w_instock` in [0,1] · V5 `shelf_instock_hours <= pod_instock_hours` · V6 pod-NULL <=> shelf-NULL
(LAW 5) · V7 exactly one absorber per (machine, pod).

### ⚠️ R21-D3 - S-22's "perf half closed" was benchmarked on a query the engine will never run

Measuring the split view's cost exposed the parent. On the same object, same session:
`count(*)` = **3.4s**, `count(velocity_instock)` = **15.4s**. `count(*)` lets the planner elide the
`dep` CTE - the correlated per-cell case-C depletion subquery - **and** the `v_shelf_sales_identity`
join. Leg 18's "readable fleet-wide in a single statement" was measured that way.
`v_shelf_sales_identity` alone is **85ms**, so the numerator is innocent; the cost is `dep`.
The split machinery adds only **3.1s** (`v_shelf_state` itself is 122ms), giving ~19s fleet-wide.

⚠️ **This is a design constraint on P2.2, not just a note: STEP 7's S1 demands a full-fleet shadow run

### ⚠️ R22-D2 - the harness reported a GREEN run that evaluated NOTHING

First `run_all('P2')` returned **`0 pass / 0 fail / passed = true`**. Not a fixture bug - a harness
bug, and the most dangerous result a proof harness can produce, because every downstream LAW-8
decision reads it as evidence.

**Two defects, one inside the other.** (1) `run_all(p_phase)` filters the FIXTURE set by phase but
called `run_fixture(id, note)` **without** it, so the gate fell back to `config.current_phase='P1'`
and every P2 assertion was skipped. As shipped, `run_all('P2')` could never have evaluated a single
P2 assertion. (2) The harness already refused to call an empty _fixture_ set green ("Guard 2: an
empty run is never a pass") but had **no equivalent one level down** for an empty _assertion_ set.
Fixed by `…185938` (pass-through + **Guard 3**), which also advances `config.current_phase` P1 → P2 -
the honest value, since Phases 0 and 1 are CLOSED.

⚠️ **And the first fix was itself wrong, caught before it was trusted.** `GREATEST(COALESCE(p_phase,
fixture_phase), fixture_phase)` is wrong _downward_: `run_all('P0')` would have gated fixture 3 at
`P0` and skipped its 9 P1 assertions - **14 evaluated silently becoming 5**, a coverage LOSS dressed
as a green run, i.e. the exact class Guard 3 had just been added to catch, reintroduced by the fix
for it. `…190011` states the semantics explicitly - `p_phase` is a **filter, not a ceiling**, and the
gate is the max of `p_phase`, the config phase and the fixture's own phase, so **the gate is
monotone: no argument to `run_all` can reduce coverage.**

### ⚠️ R22-D3 - waking 4 dormant assertions jammed LAW 8, and the fix is evidence-based

Advancing to P2 woke **4 assertions that had never once been evaluated** (fixture 3 ×2, fixture 5,
fixture 105). Three fail - and they are supposed to. Their own descriptions say **"RED until P2"**,
**"ENABLED AT P2.5, red until then"**, "Needs `engine_add_pod_v3` to consume `product_sourcing`".
They are **acceptance criteria for an engine that does not exist**, not regressions.

That is a genuine conflict with the loop's own machinery: **LAW 8 halts phase work on any golden
failure**, so `run_all('P0')` could never be green again until late Phase 2, and the human response
to a permanently-red suite is to stop reading it. The harness had no way to say "expected red until
X exists" - the fixtures expressed it in **prose, inside description strings, where no runner can
read it**.

`…190326` makes it first-class: `golden.assertions.acceptance_gate_sql`, a nullable boolean SQL.
NULL = ordinary tripwire, a failure is a failure. Returns FALSE = the subject is not built, so a
failure counts as `expected_red`, not `fail`. Returns TRUE = **binding from that moment on, with no
migration and nobody having to remember.** Deliberately **evidence-based rather than a phase label**:
the harness vocabulary is P0..P5 and cannot express "P2.5", which is exactly where two of these land.
A broken gate **fails closed** (treated as binding) so it can never silence a real failure. A
passing expected-red assertion is flagged `arrived_early` - information, not an error.

📌 **One already is.** Fixture 3 seq 4 (the P2.5 unconditional empty-shelf floor) **passes today**
on the v19 engine. Worth knowing before P2.5 is built: either the floor already holds incidentally,
or the assertion is weaker than intended. Recorded, not acted on.

### ⛔ R24-D1 - THE PHASE-2 ACCEPTANCE CONTRACT WAS UNSATISFIABLE, and the engine would have taken the blame

The pointer's NEXT TASK was `engine_add_pod_v3`. Before writing a line of engine SQL I read the seven
gated assertions' `check_sql` column by column. **Every one of them reads `public.pod_refills` or
`public.blocked_demand`. Not one reads `pod_refill_plan`.**

| Assertion          | Reads                                                       |
| ------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------- |
| fixture 3 seq 1    | `pod_refills` - NOT EXISTS coverage probe                   |
| fixture 3 seq 4    | `pod_refills.qty`                                           |
| fixture 5 seq 10   | `pod_refills.clamp_reason = 'blocked_no_wh'`                |
| fixture 14 seq 30  | `pod_refills` - NOT EXISTS coverage probe                   |
| fixture 14 seq 31  | `pod_refills.current_stock <= pod_refills.max_stock`        |
| fixture 14 seq 32  | `pod_refills.qty = 0 AND pod_refills.clamp_reason NOT NULL` |
| fixture 105 seq 10 | `blocked_demand.reason = 'blocked_no_wh'`                   |

**`pod_refill_plan_shadow` has no `current_stock`, no `max_stock`, no `clamp_reason`, no
`wh_available_pod`.** It mirrors `pod_refill_plan` - the plan/approval grain (action, status,
approval) - not `pod_refills`, the engine-advisory grain. So the object `engine_add_pod_v3` was told
to write **cannot express the contract it was told to satisfy**, and LAW 4 forbids the only
alternative (writing the live table).

⚠️ **What would have happened had I built the engine first.** All seven gates arm on
`EXISTS(pg_proc WHERE proname='engine_add_pod_v3')`. The instant the function existed, six assertions
would have flipped from `expected_red` to genuine **FAIL**, LAW 8 would have fired, and the next leg
would have bisected an engine that was **not at fault** - the defect was in the table it was pointed
at. The pointer explicitly warned "expect the suite to go red the moment the function is created…
that is designed behaviour, not a regression", which would have made the real defect _look expected_.

### ✅ R24-U1 - `pod_refills_shadow` + `v_blocked_demand_shadow_v3` (4 migrations, Dara → Cody → apply)

**Dara's design, three judgment calls each with a stated "when this is wrong":**

- **`velocity_30d` deliberately NOT mirrored** (S-13: units-per-day despite the name, read three
  incompatible ways by v19). Copying a known-defective field into a clean object propagates the
  defect. The shadow carries `velocity_instock`, daily by construction. Wrong if a later leg needs a
  field-by-field velocity diff - then add it back additively, cheap because the table is new.
- **`availability_basis` NOT NULL, new.** v19 collapses "unknown" and "unconstrained" onto the same
  encoding (`wh_available_pod IS NULL`). Under P1.1 sourcing those are **opposite meanings**, and
  fixture 5/105 seq 10 is exactly the assertion that ambiguity defeats.
- **No CHECK on the `clamp_reason` vocabulary** - 14 values live today and P2.5 must add at least one
  more. A value list would freeze the vocabulary the phase exists to extend.

**Cody: ⚠️ Approve with revisions - FOUR, all applied before apply:**

1. **`ON DELETE RESTRICT` → NO ACTION** on all three FKs. Principle worth keeping: _a shadow must
   never constrain production more tightly than the live twin it shadows._
2. **`BEFORE UPDATE OR DELETE` trigger.** `CREATE POLICY … FOR UPDATE USING (false)` binds
   `authenticated` only and is bypassed by the SECURITY DEFINER writer and `service_role` - i.e. by
   exactly the two identities that will ever write it. ADR §5 guarantee (1) is load-bearing for the
   Article 14 signoff, so it needed enforcement that binds the writer.
3. **`availability_basis='unknown'` must carry a `clamp_reason`** - otherwise the column added to
   close a LAW-5 gap becomes a LAW-5 escape hatch.
4. **Extend the seq-91 tripwire to three live tables** before the engine exists.

📌 **THE BEST THING IN THIS UNIT: LAW 5 as a CHECK constraint.** `CHECK (qty > 0 OR clamp_reason IS
NOT NULL)` makes a silent zero **unrepresentable** rather than merely detectable. Safe to impose only
because it was measured first: across all **3,841** live `pod_refills` rows, **834** have `qty = 0`
and **zero** have a NULL `clamp_reason` - true over the entire history of the mirrored table, so not
a novel restriction. Two siblings do the same for availability. **Where a law can be made
unrepresentable, prefer that to asserting it in a fixture.**

**Proof is behavioural, not structural - 10 of 10 inside one rollback envelope:** valid INSERT
accepted · **UPDATE refused** · **DELETE refused** · silent `qty=0` refused · `qty=0` **with**
`clamp_reason` accepted · `boonz_wh` + NULL availability refused · **`venue` + NULL availability
accepted** (unconstrained is legal and must stay legal) · `unknown` without reason refused · same
natural key under a **new `run_id` accepted** (re-runs additive, ADR §2) · duplicate inside one
`run_id` refused. **Residue after rollback: 0 rows.**

**Blocked demand in shadow is a VIEW, and the distinction is constitutional.** `_blocked_demand_gaps_v3`
is a pure SELECT with no state, and the shadow rows it reads are already durable and immutable
(ADR §5.1), so Article 14's first clause **genuinely binds** - the exact opposite of the shadow
table's own case, where the inputs vanish by morning. Table where staleness is real, view where it is
not. Exclusion list reproduced verbatim; `velocity_instock` emitted under its **own** key rather than
reusing `velocity_30d` with a different quantity behind it.

📌 **TRAP THAT COST ONE REPAIR THIS LEG, and it will recur - read before writing the next baseline.**
An `Edit` on `PRD-110-EXECUTION-LOG.md` fires a **PostToolUse formatter hook** (prettier) that
reflows the markdown _after_ the write. Leg 25 wrote the baseline block, then used `Edit` to tidy a
padded line number on the hash line itself - the formatter then reflowed lines **1..6391** and the
just-recorded scoped hash was **stale on arrival** (`efabc587…` recorded vs `b4f9f44f…` true). It was
caught only because the hook announced itself and the hash was re-measured.
**Rule: compute and write the EXECUTION-LOG scoped hash LAST, via `bash` (`cat >>` / `sed`), never
via `Edit`/`Write` - and if any hooked tool touches the file afterwards, re-measure and re-record.**
The sibling trap is that `wc -l <file` on macOS emits leading spaces, so `printf '…1..%s…' "$N"`
writes `1..6391`; use `awk '{print $1}'` or `$(( ))` to strip it.

⚠️ **CORRECTION to the trap note above, found by re-verifying the baseline instead of trusting it.**
The formatter hook does **not** touch only the file passed to `Edit` - it reformatted **every modified
markdown file in the working tree**. `MIGRATIONS_REGISTRY.md` and `PARKING-LOT.md` had been appended
via `bash` (no hook) and hashed _before_ the `Edit` fired; both hashes were **stale** by the time the
block was written, and only a full re-verification caught it. Three hashes had to be re-recorded, not
one. **Standing rule: after the last hooked tool call of the leg, re-verify the ENTIRE baseline block
and re-record every drifted entry - then recompute the scoped EXECUTION-LOG hash last, because fixing
any file line inside the block changes lines 1..N.** Final state verified: **all 24 file hashes MATCH**
and the scoped hash `853ef0c4…` matches its own recomputation.

## ⛔ R26-D1 — THE POINTER'S "RECOMMENDED" NEXT MOVE WOULD HAVE MANUFACTURED TWO VACUOUS GREENS

The leg-25 pointer's item 2 offered option **(a)** "re-express all seven acceptance criteria against
the shadow objects first, as its own atomic unit — **recommended**" or **(b)** engine + re-expression
in ONE unit. I measured the premise before acting on it (LAW 13), by reading all seven assertions and
all four fixture scenarios.

**All four fixtures call `public.engine_add_pod({{plan_date}}, 7)` — the v19 engine — writing live
`pod_refills`.** So re-pointing the assertions at the shadow objects without a v3 call in the
scenario leaves them reading an **empty table**, and the instant the engine exists and the gates open:

- fixture 3 seq 1 and 14 seq 30/31/32 ("count of uncovered shelves = 0") fail genuinely;
- **fixture 5 seq 10 and 105 seq 10 ("count of blocked = 0") pass VACUOUSLY** — an empty table has
  zero bad rows. That is the S-29 class reintroduced by the migration meant to arm these;
- **fixture 3 seq 4 REGRESSES** — it is today's single arrived-early PASS (`max(qty) > 0`), and
  against an empty shadow it reads 0 and turns red. The pointer itself required it must not regress.

**Option (a) is refused; option (b) is the route.** Recorded as **RISK 78**. The re-expression belongs
in the same atomic unit as the engine, and each re-expressed assertion needs a seq-89-class premise
that the v3 call actually wrote shadow rows before it asserts anything about their content.

## ⚠️ R26-D2 — MY OWN MIGRATION SHIPPED A PRIVILEGE REGRESSION, CAUGHT BY VERIFYING NOT TRUSTING

`apply_migration` returned `success: true`. Reading `proacl` afterwards showed the recreated function
carrying **`anon=X`**, which the dropped one did **not** have.

The migration **did** run `REVOKE ALL … FROM PUBLIC`. That does nothing here: **PUBLIC is not `anon`.**
Supabase's `ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES … GRANT EXECUTE ON FUNCTIONS TO anon, authenticated,
service_role` re-attaches the grant to every newly created function.

**It was not cosmetic.** The estimator's role check is `IF v_actor IS NOT NULL AND NOT EXISTS(…)`, so
for an anonymous caller `auth.uid()` is NULL and the check is **skipped entirely** — and `p_dry_run` is
only a default, so `estimate_shelf_composition_v3(<shelf>, false)` would have written real
`inventory_events` on a production shelf.

Fixed forward by **`20260730212013_prd110_p14_estimator_revoke_anon_default_priv_regression`**, which
restores the exact pre-S-28 ACL and then **asserts** it. Recorded as **RISK 77** — the mirror image of
RISK 73 (there, revoking `anon` alone missed `authenticated` on a view). **Neither revoke implies the
other; assert the whole ACL.**

## 📌 R26-D3 — THE FIRST FORCE PROBE PROVED NOTHING, AND THAT IS THE INTERESTING PART

The first probe called the estimator on a shelf cron 44 had already processed and read
`already_processed_skipped = 0` on all three calls — which reads like the guard failing.

It is not. The skip test is `EXISTS(inventory_events WHERE shelf_id = s AND source_ref = v_ref)`, and
**the idempotency marker is the EVENTS THEMSELVES, not a watermark.** A new WEIMI snapshot had landed,
and in any case **a shelf whose delta is 0 writes no event and therefore leaves no marker**, so it is
legitimately re-examined on every run. The probe never reached the branch under test — it would have
reported "force works" while exercising none of it.

**This is RISK 75's family one level down:** the fixture's own call ran, but the _branch_ under test
never executed. Recorded as **RISK 76**.

**The probe that actually proves it** — perturb belief so a real drop exists, then consume, repeat,
perturb, force (all inside a rollback envelope):

| call            |                                             result | meaning                                |
| --------------- | -------------------------------------------------: | -------------------------------------- |
| consume         |                                 `events=1 drops=1` | writes the marker under this snapshot  |
| repeat          |                           **`skipped=1 events=0`** | **idempotency PRESERVED for the cron** |
| perturb, repeat |                           **`skipped=1 events=0`** | guard still binds after perturbation   |
| **force**       | **`skipped=0 forced_rederive=1 events=1 drops=1`** | **re-derive works and does real work** |

Residue **0**: events/composition/anomalies **31 / 31 / 10** before and after, identical.

R26-D1 concluded that the leg-25 pointer's option (a) "cannot be done standalone". **That is

measured and engineered around it: every re-expressed assertion returns a sentinel **`-1`** when the
fixture has no v3 run of its own — which fails `eq 0` and `gt 0` alike, so an empty shadow table can
never read as a pass — plus a new **seq 88** run-time premise (the engine's analogue of seq 89,
self-diagnosing with `helper_never_ran` / `engine_error: <SQLERRM>`).

**The accurate statement, which supersedes RISK 78's wording:** re-expressing the seven against the
shadow objects standalone is viable **only if every re-expressed assertion carries a vacuous-green
sentinel and a run-time premise**. Done _naively_ — the mechanical swap the pointer described — it
manufactures two vacuous greens (fixture 5 seq 10, 105 seq 10) and regresses the one arrived-early
pass (fixture 3 seq 4). My measurement of that hazard stands; my conclusion that no standalone route
exists does not.

📌 **The lesson worth carrying:** I verified the pointer's claim against the code and the data, which
was right, but I did not verify it against **the working tree**. `git status` is part of STEP R, not
part of leg close.

## ✅ R27-U1 — S-28 CLOSED (4 migrations, Cody-reviewed)

`golden.arrange_shelf(shelf_id, release_snapshot)` resets DERIVED `shelf_composition` for one
shelf and re-dates that machine's newest WEIMI row, giving a fixture ownership of its own
preconditions. Fixtures 20/21/22 wired to call it. **Not one assertion was edited** — if the
arrange step is right, every existing assertion is right in BOTH worlds, which is the proof that
these fixtures were always asserting the correct thing and merely borrowing preconditions they
did not own.

**Cody: ⚠️ Approve with revisions — Articles 1, 2, 3, 4, 7, 8, 12, 13, 14, 16. Both applied.**

1. **Article 4** — `shelf_composition` carries `tg_audit_shelf_composition` → `audit_log_write`,
   a **logger, not a gate**: the DELETE succeeds but lands an **unattributed** row in
   `write_audit_log`. Now stamps `app.via_rpc`/`app.rpc_name` **and restores the prior values
   before returning** (the PRD-016B provenance-GUC leak would otherwise stamp every later write
   in the same fixture).
2. **Article 1/8** — `weimi_device_status` has **no canonical writer function** (the n8n ingest
   writes it directly) and **no triggers of any kind**, so writes there are invisible to
   `write_audit_log`. Documented in the `COMMENT` rather than left implicit.
   Cody also noted containment is **stronger** than the draft claimed: the `golden` schema ACL is
   `{postgres=UC/postgres}`, so `anon`/`authenticated` have no USAGE and cannot reach the
   function at all. The REVOKEs stay as belt-and-braces (RISK 77).

**Fixture-only guard, new at leg 27** (the leg-24 draft asserted the envelope in prose only): the
function refuses unless a `golden.runs` row with `finished_at IS NULL` is visible. `run_fixture`
inserts that row before executing the scenario and finishes it in the same transaction, so it
exists **iff** a golden run is in flight; no production path ever has one. The migration proves
the guard binds by calling the function and requiring the exception.

## ⚠️ R27-D3 — THE LEG-24 FILE'S CODE COULD NEVER HAVE RUN, AND ONLY RUNNING IT SHOWED THAT

Its snapshot release **INSERTs** a replay row into `weimi_device_status`. That table carries
`unique_device_status UNIQUE (weimi_device_id, snapshot_date)` — **one row per device per DAY**.
So the replay collides with the row it copied, on every call, on any date the device already
reported. Fixtures 20 and 22 raised `duplicate key value violates unique constraint`.

📌 **The reasoning was sound and the code was impossible.** S-31 is S-30's mirror image twice
over: a file without an apply, whose _analysis_ was better than three subsequent legs' and whose
_implementation_ had never executed once.

**Fixed by re-dating the existing row instead of inserting one** — which is also strictly better:
no row is added to the sensor table, no stock number is touched, and Cody's Article 1/8 concern
shrinks to a single-column UPDATE inside a rollback envelope.

## ⚠️ R27-D4 — MY OWN FIX SHIPPED A TYPE BUG, AND IT HID BEHIND A HARNESS HOLE (S-33)

I declared `v_status bigint`; `weimi_device_status.status_id` is **uuid**. Every call raised
`invalid input syntax for type bigint`. That should have been obvious and was not, because:

**`golden.run_fixture` catches a scenario error into `detail` and keeps evaluating assertions.**
The scenario's own `golden.scratch` DELETE+INSERT rolls back with it, so **every assertion then
reads the PREVIOUS run's scratch and passes on stale data.** Fixture 20 reported **20 passes**
while its scenario had aborted and `written_at` still showed a run 20 minutes earlier. Worse, my
own analysis query filtered `jsonb_array_elements(detail) WHERE e ? 'seq'` — and the
`scenario_error` element **has no `seq`**, so it was invisible to exactly the query I was using
to look for failures. Recorded as **S-33**; the fixture is not reported green (the error counts
as a fail) but the passes are fictional.

Cody-reviewed, **4 revisions demanded and applied** (R1 `machine_id` as PK — a `status_id` PK turned

restore commit atomically and no other session can observe the pinned value — which is what makes the
cron-44 estimator race **impossible** rather than unlikely.

flight · negative REFUSED · restore-without-pin REFUSED · 16 aisles, **204 → 0 → 204** · per-shelf
fingerprint byte-identical · `snapshot_at` untouched · backup 1 → 0 · residue 0.
ACL measured `{postgres=X, service_role=X}`, exactly 1 overload each.

### L29-6 · ⚠️ RISK 85 (found while closing) — the formatter hook silently rewrites SIBLING docs

Editing **one** file (`PRD-110-PARKING-LOT.md`) fired a `PostToolUse` formatter that also rewrote
**`MIGRATIONS_REGISTRY.md` and `RPC_REGISTRY.md`**, which this leg never touched. Attributed by
mtime, not guessed: `02:19:56`, `02:19:57`, `02:19:59` local — one burst — while
`METRICS_REGISTRY.md` still carries leg 28's `23:44:29`.

**Both files' SHA-256 matched leg 28's recorded baseline exactly at STEP R and differ at close**
(`06dc6454… → 30760316…`, `5f9069f7… → 0e44dcde…`). **Content verified intact, not assumed:**
MIGRATIONS_REGISTRY 1531 lines / 233224 non-space chars with its leg-27 and leg-28 sections both
present; RPC_REGISTRY 678 lines / 169672 non-space chars with `pin_machine_stock`, `arrange_shelf`
and `estimate_shelf_composition_v3` all still registered. The change is reflow, not loss.

📌 **Consequence for the relay, and it is the point: a hash mismatch at STEP R does NOT by itself
mean a concurrent session edited the file.** The formatter can move any doc's hash as a side effect
of editing an unrelated one. Next leg: if a doc hash moves but its line/word/non-space-char counts
and section markers are intact, suspect the formatter first. This is the known Cursor
formatter-noise gotcha (PRD-072 / PRD-071) reaching the PRD-110 hash baseline.
⚠️ **Also: `wc -l` on macOS pads its output with spaces** — `head -"$(wc -l < f)"` fails and, piped
into `shasum`, silently yields `e3b0c442…`, the SHA-256 of the **empty string**. That is a parity
check that reports a confident hash for nothing at all (RISK 79's family). Use `tr -d ' '`.

SECURITY DEFINER, `(p_plan_date date, p_days_cover integer) RETURNS jsonb`, `anon` REVOKEd,
`search_path` pinned. Preamble exactly as contracted: Article 4 provenance → role check →
`_assert_refill_plan_writable(p_plan_date)` **one-arg as v19 calls it** → picked-machines check →
`_assert_gate_zero` (LAW 11 binds the shadow engine too).

machines. R29-D1 confirmed in practice: v3 inherits none of S-35's ~17h/day blindness.

⭐ **The defect it exists to close is one predicate.** v19 inserts
`WHERE (NOT f.is_dead AND f.need_raw > 0)`, so a shelf whose need rounds to 0, an over-capacity shelf
and a dead-tagged shelf get **no row at all**. v3 emits a line for **every** in-scope pod-bound shelf

any in-scope shelf got no line or if `lines <> scope`. A short run fails loudly instead of returning a
cheerful number.

### L32-3 · ⛔ S-37 — the split view joins a raw pod key against a canonical one

`v_shelf_sales_identity` and `v_shelf_instock_velocity_v3` both apply a hardcoded alias
(`168aeb7e` `Hunter` → `51e4600f` `Hunter Ridge`). **`v_shelf_instock_velocity_split_v3` does not** — the
shelf-grain object the engine will read. Its final join takes `f.pod_product_id` from `v_shelf_state`
(**raw**) against `v.pod_product_id` (**already canonical**), misses, and 16 shelves get NULL.

**The data was never missing:** all 16 machines have a canonical velocity row, **15 of 16 non-null**
(mean **0.3042** u/day), and the canonical key carries **216 units_30d** across 20 rows. Third instance
of the S-04 / S-19 / S-36 family — a join predicate is a hypothesis, and this one is falsified by the
data it reads.

⛔ **The trap, found before writing any fix:** weights partition by the **raw** pod while velocity is
computed on the **canonical** pod, and **7 of the 16 machines carry BOTH a Hunter and a Hunter Ridge
shelf**. A one-line join fix double-counts on **14 shelves**. The key must be canonicalised in the
`shelves` CTE _and_ in `slot_stock` (raw WEIMI history), so the merged group shares one velocity pool.

✅ **Dry-run proven, read-only:** the corrected logic merges the family to **26 shelves**, **24 of 26**
recover non-null velocity (the 2 that stay NULL are AMZ-1046 = D-13), and conservation is **exact** —
max |Σw − 1| = **0.000000000**, **0 pods violating**, measured across every pod group in the full
544-shelf population, not just the family.

### L32-4 · ⏸️ D-13 — a live, selling machine hidden from every canonical sales metric by stale metadata

`is_eligible_machine` is an **Adyen-telemetry** predicate, not a refill-scope one:
`adyen_status='Online today' AND adyen_inventory_in_store='Live' AND` repurpose-grace. AMZ-1046 reads
`'Switched off'` / `'Pending Setup'`, so all 16 rows fail it — and eligibility is the **only** predicate
that fails (`enabled=16 notbroken=16 eligible=0 haspod=16`).

The machine is demonstrably live: `Active`, `include_in_refill=true`, `fully_managed`, 16/16 in
`v_shelf_availability_v3`, **28 sales in 30 days (latest 2026-07-30 17:27 UTC)**, 33 units of WEIMI
movement. It is the **only** Active + in-refill machine fleet-wide failing the predicate. Not fixed
here on purpose: `machines` is protected (LAW 3) and adyen-sync can revert a manual re-stamp.

### L33-1 · ⛔ The trap in S-37, found before writing the fix — and leg 32's proof could not have caught it

Leg 32 dry-ran a canonicalisation and reported conservation **exact** (max |Σw − 1| =
**0.000000000**, **0** pods violating, all 544). That is real evidence and it is **not sufficient.**

The view carries a **residual absorber**: `w_instock = w_raw + (1 − w_sum)` on `absorber_rank = 1`.
Σw is forced to exactly 1 **whatever the partition key is**. _A conservation identity enforced by an
absorber can never falsify the key it is computed over._

What it hid: `v_shelf_state` derives `pod_shelf_count` as
`count(*) OVER (PARTITION BY b.machine_id, i.pod_product_id)` — the **RAW** key — and **all 26**
family shelves carry `n = 1` (measured, all 26 listed). Canonicalising only the partition keys merges
two shelves that each still believe `n = 1`: both take `single_shelf` (`w_raw = 1.0`), `w_sum` = 2.0,
and the absorber "repairs" the pair to **w = 0.0 and w = 1.0**. One real shelf gets **zero** velocity
— a **LAW 5 silent zero behind a green conservation check**, on all **7** dual machines.

So the fix is **three** edits, not one: canonicalise in `shelves`, canonicalise in `slot_stock`, and
**recompute `n` over the merged group**.

### L33-2 · Fixture first (LAW 1), and the failing baseline captured before any fix

`20260731005200` added 5 assertions to fixture 2 (seq 60–64) riding the **single existing read** of
the split view — **zero extra evaluations** (S-26; a separate fixture would have added another full
~35 s evaluation of the most expensive object in the schema to every suite run). Caught before apply:
the harness comparator's operator is **`lte`, not `le`** — `le` RAISEs, and `run_fixture` catches the
raise into `passed=false`, so it would have **masqueraded as the intended expected-red**.

**Failing baseline, recorded:** seq 60 = **16** (raw-keyed rows) · seq 61 = **17** family shelves with
NULL velocity (16 Hunter join-misses + AMZ-1046's Hunter Ridge) · seq 62/63 = **0** · seq 64 = **26**.

The first run came back `n_pass 44 / n_fail 2 / n_expected_red 2`. The 2 hard fails were **seq 92/93**,

with `'pr'` (`pod_refills`) and `'bd'` (`blocked_demand`), so rebuilding from the file silently
reverted leg 24's work and both tripwires read a missing key.

**A migration file is a record of one change, never the current state of a mutable row.** Repaired in
the same atomic unit (`20260731010500`, anchored `replace()` + a `RAISE` if the anchor moves), and the
general guard is now shipped in that migration's header — run it before AND after any `scenario_sql`
edit:

```sql
WITH refs AS (SELECT DISTINCT (regexp_matches(check_sql,'value->>''([a-z0-9_]+)''','g'))[1] k
              FROM golden.assertions WHERE fixture_id = N),
     have AS (SELECT DISTINCT jsonb_object_keys(value) k FROM golden.scratch WHERE fixture_id = N)
SELECT refs.k FROM refs LEFT JOIN have USING (k) WHERE have.k IS NULL;   -- must be EMPTY
```

Re-captured clean: **46 pass / 0 fail / 2 expected-red**, both mine, exactly as designed.

### [leg 36 · L36-2] ⛔ S-41 · anomalies accrue PER CRON FIRING, not per snapshot - leg 25's rate is 24x low

Counting the burn-in's anomalies for L36-1 surfaced a number that did not fit leg 25's model.
Leg 25 recorded anomalies as raised "**once per snapshot per offending shelf**" and projected
"5 rows per snapshot on one machine, 41 per snapshot fleet-wide, roughly daily". The live data:
**35 rows across only 4 distinct `weimi_snapshot_at` values.**

The decomposition, and it is unambiguous:

| `weimi_snapshot_at`      | rows raised | shelves | cron firings that processed it     |
| ------------------------ | ----------- | ------- | ---------------------------------- |
| 2026-07-30 18:00:36Z     | 5           | 5       | 1 (18:40)                          |
| 2026-07-30 19:59:08Z     | 5           | 5       | 1 (20:40)                          |
| 2026-07-30 21:32:11Z     | 5           | 5       | 1 (21:40)                          |
| **2026-07-30 22:00:40Z** | **20**      | **5**   | **4 (22:40, 23:40, 00:40, 01:40)** |

Per shelf on that last snapshot: `times_raised = 4`, `distinct (observed_qty, expected_qty)` = **1**.
Byte-identical rows, four times, for one observation. WEIMI simply delivered no new snapshot for
3h40m and the estimator re-raised the same five anomalies on every firing.

**The correct model: one anomaly row per offending shelf per CRON FIRING, independent of whether the
snapshot is new.** Consequences, and the third is why this is not cosmetic:

1. **The real accrual rate is 24x leg 25's figure** - 5 × 24 = **~120 rows/day** on one machine today;
   41 × 24 = **~984 rows/day** fleet-wide after the flip, roughly **30k/month**, for a condition that
   is known, expected and never auto-resolved. Leg 25's "8.2x multiplier" understates the flip's
   effect on this table by another 24x on top.
2. **`inventory_events` is unaffected** - 31, flat across all 7 firings. RISK 76 predicted exactly
   this asymmetry (the estimator's idempotency marker is the EVENTS), and it holds. The defect is
   confined to the anomaly path, which has no such marker.
3. ⛔ **An anomaly count now measures cron frequency, not reality.** Any consumer that counts,
   ages or rates-limits on `inventory_anomalies` reads a number that changes if the schedule
   changes and re-reports one physical condition as many. P4.5's scoreboard is specced to surface
   anomaly counts; on today's behaviour that metric would lie by a factor set by `40 * * * *`.

**Not a correctness fault in composition or events, and D-08 day 2 still passes** - the anomalies are
explainable, which is the criterion. But this is a metric that lies, and the fleet flip multiplies it.
**Parked as S-41 and treated as a second gate on the fleet flip alongside S-32.** Fixed FIXTURE
FIRST in L36-3 below, per LAW 1.

### [leg 36 · L36-2b] ⛔ S-41 ROOT-CAUSED, and it has a SECOND symptom that lands in 16 hours

**Root cause, confirmed empirically and read-only** (dry run on one MPMCC-1058 shelf, zero writes):

```
already_processed_skipped: 0   <-- on a snapshot ALREADY processed four times
shelves_flat: 1                <-- flat, so no event is written
sensor_above_capacity: 1       <-- and the anomaly would be raised again
```

The estimator's idempotency guard is
`IF EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM inventory_events WHERE shelf_id = s.shelf_id AND source_ref = v_ref)`.
A sensor-lie shelf clamps to capacity, its belief already equals the clamped count, so `v_delta = 0`,
so it takes the `n_flat` branch and **writes no event**. The marker is the event; no event means no
marker; no marker means it never skips. **This is RISK 76 exactly** ("the estimator's idempotency
marker is the EVENTS, so a flat shelf never skips") - previously recorded as a note, now measured
with a cost. Every flat shelf re-runs its entire body on every one of the 24 daily firings.

⛔ **SECOND SYMPTOM, previously unrecorded, and it is the serious one.** The loop tail runs
unconditionally for every non-skipped shelf:

```sql
v_days  := (now() - COALESCE(max(last_verified_at), min(created_at))) / 1 day;
IF v_days > 1 THEN
  v_decay := LEAST(1.0, composition_decay_per_day * v_days);
  PERFORM decay_composition_confidence_v3(shelf_id, v_decay, 'age decay');   -- SUBTRACTS v_decay
END IF;
```

`decay_composition_confidence_v3` **subtracts**: `confidence := GREATEST(0, LEAST(1, confidence - p_amount))`.
So the tail subtracts an amount proportional to **total elapsed days measured from a FIXED anchor**,
**once per firing**. Two independent defects compound:

|          | defect                                                                                                  | consequence                                                                     |
| -------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **S-41** | no marker for flat shelves ⇒ tail runs **24x/day**, not once                                            | decay rate 24x intended                                                         |
| **S-42** | the tail **subtracts `rate × total_days`** from a fixed anchor instead of decaying once per elapsed day | decay is **cumulative/quadratic in time**, wrong even at a once-per-day cadence |

**Measured, not projected.** All 31 composition rows sit at `confidence = 0.30` (the cold-start
value) with `last_verified_at IS NULL` and `min(created_at) = 2026-07-30 18:40:00Z`, so the anchor
is fixed and `v_days > 1` is still false - which is the only reason nothing has decayed yet.

⏰ **`v_days` crosses 1 at 2026-07-31 18:40:00 UTC - in 16h31m.** The 19:40 firing is the first that
decays. At `composition_decay_per_day = 0.02` the first subtraction is 0.0200 per firing and grows
with `v_days`; from 0.30 that is **~15 firings to zero, ≈0.63 days**. **Every composition row on the
burn-in machine reaches `confidence = 0` by ~2026-08-01 09:00 UTC** - i.e. _before_ D-08's day-3
check on ~2026-08-02, and the day-3 observer would find a fleet of zero-confidence beliefs and no
obvious cause.

**Why this outranks P2.2 for this leg.** `composition_confidence_min_autoaction = 0.70` gates expiry
auto-write-off lines (BUILD SPEC P1.4); `composition_confidence_prompt_threshold = 0.50` gates the
driver-collapse prompts. Confidence pinned at 0 disables **both**, permanently and silently, on a
cron CS has already activated - and the D-08 fleet flip is 2 days out, which multiplies it by 8.2x.
This is a live defect in shipped, CS-activated code with a known landing time; P2.2 is greenfield
work that will wait one leg. **Fixed FIXTURE FIRST below (LAW 1).**

### [leg 37 · L37-2] ⛔ P2.2 PROBED BEFORE DESIGNING — and the BUILD SPEC's named input is a STALE SEED

The leg-37 pointer required probing `machine_service_policy` / `machine_class` before designing,
because BUILD SPEC P2.2 names them but neither had ever been verified live. **All three of this
leg's findings would have silently corrupted P2.2 had it been built as written.**

**1. The dependency EXISTS, and so do the service-level parameters.**
`machine_service_policy` is a real table (`relkind='r'`), **30 rows**, columns
`machine_id, machine_class, trip_interval_days, z_default, source, notes`. `refill_policy_params`
already carries **`z_low 1.28 / z_mid 1.65 / z_high 2.05`** and `cold_start_days 14`.
**No Dara escalation is needed for the parameter surface** - it is already designed.

**2. ⛔ `trip_interval_days` OVERSTATES REAL VISIT CADENCE BY 1.8x-3.9x.** The table is a
`source='seed_velocity_tertile'` seed from 2026-06-21 - an exact 10/10/10 tertile split, never
curated. `z_default` is the **constant 1.65** on all 30 rows, so it does not vary by
`machine_class` at all despite BUILD SPEC saying "z ... join by machine_class".
Observed cadence, re-derived from `refill_dispatching` (executed-visit evidence
`picked_up|dispatched|returned|packed`, non-cancelled, 120-day window, median inter-visit gap):

| machine_class | policy `trip_interval_days` | observed median gap (avg) | range      | overstatement |
| ------------- | --------------------------- | ------------------------- | ---------- | ------------- |
| backup        | 30                          | **9.00**                  | 4.0 – 20.5 | **3.3x**      |
| busy          | 12                          | **6.80**                  | 2.0 – 11.0 | **1.8x**      |
| standard      | 21                          | **5.45**                  | 2.5 – 8.0  | **3.9x**      |

Corroborated independently: **max `days_since_visit` fleet-wide is 16 days**, yet 10 machines are
seeded at a 30-day interval.

⛔ **Why this is the dangerous kind of wrong.** `S = μ·L + z·σ√L` with `L` 3.9x too large inflates
`S` ~4x. The engine then computes
`need_raw = LEAST(GREATEST(cover_units, floor_units), fill_to_cap)`, so the inflated `S` is
**absorbed by `fill_to_cap`** - every shelf simply fills to capacity, every visit. There is **no
error, no exception, no qty-0, no clamp_reason anomaly**: v3 would look healthy while having
silently degenerated into "always max fill", and the Phase-2 gate (**WMAPE(v3) ≤ WMAPE(v19)**)
would fail with no visible cause. Recorded as **S-43**.

**3. ⛔ THE σ SOURCE HAS A LITERAL THAT SILENTLY RETURNS ZERO ROWS.** The daily-demand series for σ
comes from `v_sales_history_resolved(transaction_id, machine_id, pod_product_id, transaction_date,
qty, delivery_status)`. The plausible-looking filter `delivery_status = 'Success'` returns
**`actual rows=0`** - measured, via `EXPLAIN ANALYZE`, not assumed. The live vocabulary is
**`'Successful'`**, and it is the **only** value present in all 38,386 rows.
A σ built on `'Success'` would be **0 fleet-wide**, making `z·σ` vanish and turning base-stock back
into bare `μ·L` - a silent, total loss of safety stock, exactly the class LAW 5 forbids.
Recorded as **RISK 91**. Caught only by honouring the "declare no data only after checking the join
path" anti-pattern.

**4. σ's history is far sparser than the BUILD SPEC's phrasing implies.** Over 60 days at
(machine, pod) grain: **637 pairs**, 7,105 daily rows (cheap - 2.3 ms). But only **182 pairs (29%)
have ≥14 days** of sales, **310 (49%) have ≥7**, and **81 pairs have exactly ONE day**, where
`stddev_samp` is **NULL**. **The "min-history guard → archetype prior" is not an edge case - it is
the majority path (455 of 637 pairs).** Sampled dispersion, `φ = σ/√μ`: 13.05/√20.77 = **2.86**,
2.830/√7.548 = **1.03** - i.e. real demand runs 1x-3x Poisson, so a fixed prior is not defensible
and φ must itself be estimated.

📌 **A trap the next leg must not walk into.** Computing σ over _days with sales_ is wrong twice:
it drops zero-demand days, and it counts stockout days as zero demand. `velocity_instock` already
excludes empty hours (P2.1), so μ is **in-stock-corrected** while a naive σ would not be - mixing
two bases, which is the S-13 defect in a new costume. The scale-free route (`φ = σ_obs/√μ_obs`
applied to the canonical μ) is robust to this because numerator and denominator shift together.

**5. ✅ D-13's build obligation is ALREADY DISCHARGED - do not rebuild it.** D-13 states "the P2.2
branch falls back to `velocity_raw` and records the reason". Reading the live engine, that fallback
**already exists** at P2.1 (`engine_add_pod_v3` lines 126-131): `velocity_source` resolves
`instock_split` → **`weimi_raw_fallback`** → `none_no_signal`, with `vel_eff` following the same
ladder. Nothing to build; D-13 remains a **CS metadata question only**.

⚠️ **AND THE TWO GAPS ARE THE SAME MACHINE.** The one in-scope machine with **no**
`machine_service_policy` row is **`AMZ-1046-2406-O1`** (`981a155e`, 32 shelves, **16 pod-bound**) -
which is precisely **D-13's** machine. It also has **0 measurable inter-visit gaps** in 120 days.
So it has **neither a service policy NOR an observable cadence**, and P2.2 must resolve it from a
parameter default or silently starve 16 pod-bound shelves (LAW 5). This is why the resolver needs a
**three-tier** fallback, not two.

### ⛔ S-48 — the repair S-47 _specified_ would not have worked, and seq 93 was already blind

S-47 step 2 said to re-express seq 92 "the same shape as seq 93", i.e. scoped by `created_at >= t0`.
**Probed before building it, and that shape is structurally vacuous.** `pod_refills.created_at`
DEFAULTs to `now()` = **TRANSACTION START**, while `t0` is a `clock_timestamp()` taken INSIDE the
transaction. Measured: fixture 14's `t0` = **03:53:38.885165Z**, its own writes carry
`created_at = 03:52:59.546876Z`, so `created_at >= t0` is **false for the fixture's own writes**.
**seq 93 has been passing green while blind for many legs.**

Two further traps were probed rather than assumed, and both would have shipped a broken guard:

- ⛔ `xmin = pg_current_xact_id()::xid` matched **1 of 2** writes. `golden.run_fixture` executes
  `scenario_sql` inside a `BEGIN..EXCEPTION` block, i.e. a **subtransaction**. `pg_xact_status`
  matched **2 of 2**.
- ⛔ `golden.run_all` runs **every fixture in ONE transaction** (proven: all fixtures in a run share
  `created_at`). So machine-scoping was also insufficient - and **`AMZ-1046-2406-O1`, one of fixture
  14's two machines, was written by a LIVE actor 9 times today**, which would have kept the race
  alive. The tripwires are therefore stated at the honest grain: the SUITE may write only on
  registered synthetic (`>=2030`) fixture `plan_date`s.

**Fix:** `golden.written_by_this_txn(xid)` - a row visible to our snapshot whose `xmin` is still
`'in progress'` can only have been written by our own transaction tree. Plus **seq 100**, an
anti-vacuity self-test that proves every run that the predicate can actually see this run's own
writes (reads **14**). A guard that silently sees nothing is precisely what S-48 _was_.

### S-50 — root cause re-confirmed at the source, and the fix is NOT the one the parking lot assumed

Per the pointer I did **not** re-derive the diagnosis; I confirmed it at the source and then probed
for the fix. `propose_inactivate_on_zero_stock` (read live) fires only on
`NEW.status='Active' AND COALESCE(NEW.warehouse_stock,0)=0 AND COALESCE(NEW.consumer_stock,0)=0`.
The five blockers are exactly the ones S-50 names, and they carry more evidence than recorded:

| batch_id                        | warehouse_stock | consumer_stock | provenance_reason | audit rows |
| ------------------------------- | --------------- | -------------- | ----------------- | ---------- |
| `VOXSOURCE-WH_MCC-AQUAFINA-999` | 636             | **50**         | `dispatch_pack`   | 94         |
| `VOXSOURCE-WH_MCC-PEPSI-999`    | 983             | **16**         | `dispatch_pack`   | 12         |

⭐ **All five are `provenance_reason='dispatch_pack'`** — the consumer stock was minted by _packing
sentinel units into machines_. It is phantom stock derived from phantom stock, which is why the
retirement must account for it rather than route around it.

### ⭐ THE FINDING OF THIS STEP R — canonical writers already exist, and one is a naming foot-gun

A `pg_proc` scan for `consumer_stock` writers found the retirement path does **not** need a new RPC:

- ⭐ **`drain_consumer_stock_phantom(p_wh_inventory_id, p_reason, p_drained_by)`** — SECURITY DEFINER,
  role-gated (`warehouse`/`operator_admin`/`superadmin`/`manager`), **≥10-char reason**, zeroes
  `consumer_stock`, **writes `inventory_audit_log`**, sets `app.via_rpc` / `app.rpc_name` /
  `app.provenance_reason='manual_adjust'`, and raises if there is nothing to drain. **This is the
  canonical one.**
- ⛔ **`drain_phantom_consumer_stock(p_wh_inventory_id, p_units, p_reason)`** — near-identical name,
  **older and weaker**: `operator_admin`/`superadmin` only, requires a non-null `auth.uid()`, takes a
  unit count, and writes **NO audit row**. This is the CLAUDE.md `repurpose_machine` foot-gun in a new
  place. **Do NOT call it.** Recorded in PARKING-LOT as S-51.
- `drain_phantom_consumer_stock_batch_run(p_caller_id)` drives off `v_consumer_stock_leaks` — and
  ⭐ **measured live, ZERO of the 5 sentinels appear in that view** (it holds 15 rows, none of them
  sentinels). So the existing batch tool would **not** have caught this. The gap is real and uncovered.

### Ordering, established by reading the trigger rather than by trial

Drain **consumer first, warehouse second**. After the consumer drain `warehouse_stock` is still
636-992, so the trigger does not fire and no row is ever observable as _Active with zero warehouse
stock_. The subsequent `apply_inventory_correction(…,0,…)` then satisfies
`NEW.warehouse=0 ∧ NEW.consumer=0 ∧ OLD.warehouse>0` and the flip happens exactly once, provenanced.
(Warehouse-first also fires, via the `OLD.consumer_stock>0` arm, but it leaves that intermediate
window open — so it is the worse order, not merely a different one.)

### ⛔ THE FINDING OF THIS LEG — the canonical writer for this job is DEAD CODE

`drain_consumer_stock_phantom` INSERTs into `inventory_audit_log.delta`, which is
**`GENERATED ALWAYS AS (new_qty - old_qty)`** — so **every call raises `428C9`**. It has never been
able to run. Referenced by no function and no cron. And the existing batch tool would not have caught
the sentinels either: `drain_phantom_consumer_stock_batch_run` drives off `v_consumer_stock_leaks`,
and ⭐ **zero of the 5 sentinels appear in that view** (15 rows, none of them sentinels). The gap was
genuinely uncovered — which is why S-50 needed a new writer rather than a call to an existing one.

📌 A third name, `drain_phantom_consumer_stock`, **works** but is weaker (no audit row at all). Three
near-anagram names, one broken — recorded as **S-51**, retirement parked as **D-17**.

### ⭐ The apply-time proof earned its keep — the FIRST apply attempt failed on it

Per leg-42 doctrine the migration **runs** the function against a real sentinel in a rolled-back
subtransaction instead of asserting it works. That proof **rejected the first attempt**:
`app.mutation_reason` carried the `consumer_phantom_drain: ` prefix, so the generic
`trg_audit_wh_inventory` row and the explicit row became indistinguishable (`audit_rows=2` where the
semantic count had to be 1). Fixed by leaving `mutation_reason` unprefixed. **The failed apply rolled
back completely** — verified function-absent and sentinels at 40 Active / 39,377 units / 5 carriers
before re-applying. Nothing was left half-applied at any point.

📌 **Audit footprint, measured not assumed:** a consumer-only drain leaves **exactly two**
`inventory_audit_log` rows. The generic trigger reads `old_qty`/`new_qty` from **warehouse** stock, so
on a consumer-only change it records delta 0 and says nothing about what happened; the explicit row is
the only one carrying the truth.

### Ordering, established by reading the trigger rather than by trial

**Drain consumer FIRST, warehouse second.** Warehouse stock stays non-zero through the consumer loop,
so no row is ever observable as _Active with zero warehouse stock_, even transiently. Warehouse-first
also fires the trigger (via the `OLD.consumer_stock>0` arm) but leaves that window open — it is the
worse order, not merely a different one.

⭐ **R20-D1 REFINED by leg 44 (this note sits OUTSIDE the `1..N` window on purpose, so it does not
invalidate the hash above).** "Write the EXECUTION-LOG hash LAST" is not only about other FILES — the
other **five hash lines live inside this file at lines `N-5 .. N`**, i.e. inside the window the log
hash covers. Leg 44 batched all six substitutions into one `sed` pass, computed the log hash from the
still-placeholder text, and produced a hash that did not reproduce. **The correct order is: substitute
the five external hashes FIRST, then compute the log hash over `1..N`, then write ONLY line `N+1`**
(line-addressed, so nothing inside the window moves). Caught by re-verifying immediately after
writing — always re-run `head -n N | shasum` and confirm it equals what you just recorded.

⭐ **The expiry ceiling is a safety RAIL, not a re-writer.** Binding on 0.9% of shelves is the
correct shape for a ceiling, and it is the number that makes the P2.3 design safe to wire.

⛔ **A TRAP THIS MEASUREMENT CAUGHT, AND IT WOULD HAVE LOOKED LIKE A CATASTROPHE.** The first dry
run was taken against the most recent shadow run, whose `plan_date` is fixture 14's synthetic
**2030-01-15**. Every real batch in this database expires in 2026, so the ceiling read **0 on
essentially every WH-constrained line** and 29 of 33 lines "collapsed". That is not a defect — at a
2030 plan date nothing currently in the warehouse is sellable. **Any P2.3 number measured on a
synthetic 2030 plan_date is meaningless as a fleet signal.** Re-measured at `CURRENT_DATE + 1`, the

Article 8 `tg_audit_demand_calendar` was missing; Article 7 append-only was _declared but not
enforced_ (now `tg_demand_calendar_append_only`, mirroring `tg_product_sourcing_append_only`);

and `load_dow_profile_v3` was routed **through** `set_demand_factor_v3` instead of INSERTing
(Article 1). Fixture 31 seq 29-33 pin all four so they cannot silently regress.

⭐ **The most valuable thing this leg produced is a bug the fixture caught on its FIRST green run,
and it is a fully general SQL trap: a CHECK constraint PASSES when it evaluates to NULL.**
`chk_demand_calendar_shape` guarded the macro_kpi branch with `iso_week BETWEEN 1 AND 53`. With a
NULL `iso_week` that test is NULL → the branch is NULL → the disjunction is NULL → **the malformed
row was ACCEPTED**. The `dow` branch had the identical hole. Seq 6 measured `shape_rej` 2 where 3
were required. 📌 **It would have failed silently:** such a row is inert in the resolver (its
temporal predicate can never match), so the symptom is "CS authored a factor and nothing happened" —
precisely the class LAW 5 exists to forbid. Corrected **forward-only in a second migration**
(Article 12 — the applied migration was not edited), and fixture 31 was widened from 3 malformed
shapes to **5** so both halves of the hole are now pinned.

⛔ **The resolution rule is deliberately the OPPOSITE of `product_sourcing`'s, and this is the one
thing most likely to be got wrong later.** Within a source the **most specific scope wins**
(machine > class > fleet); across sources factors **multiply**; the product is then clamped to
`[demand_factor_clamp_min, demand_factor_clamp_max]` = `[0.5, 2.5]`. S-53's **ANY-SCOPE** rule
answers "who supplies this product"; this one answers "which authored factor applies". Conflating
them would double-count. Both the table comment and METRICS_REGISTRY now say so explicitly.

**Ships with an EMPTY calendar on purpose.** Zero active rows ⇒ the resolver returns exactly `1.0`
for every one of the 31 machines ⇒ **v3 quantities do not move until CS authors a factor.**
`load_dow_profile_v3` was built but deliberately **not invoked**. Fixture 31 seq 5 pins
`active_rows = 0` and is the assertion that flips, deliberately, on the first authored row.

📌 **Fixture 31 is provably non-destructive and may be re-run against production forever.** Every
probe row is written inside a PL/pgSQL subtransaction that is FORCED to roll back; PL/pgSQL variable
assignments survive the rollback, so the measurements are kept while the table is left untouched.
Seq 27 pins **zero residue**. ⭐ This idiom is the remedy S-55 needs.

enforcement + audited override)`, P2, plan_date **2030-02-03**) was written, applied, and **run RED

⭐ **Measuring the baseline before writing the fixture is what let every assertion be pinned to a

⭐ **All side effects live in `scenario_sql` and land in `golden.scratch`; every assertion is a pure
read.** Six probes run in sequence (warn · block · block+short-reason · block+override ·
block-again · block on the repaired plan). The harness helper `golden.probe_commit_under_mode` flips
`preflight_enforcement`, calls commit inside a `BEGIN…EXCEPTION` block that captures either the
result or the SQLSTATE, and **always restores the previous mode on both paths**. `run_fixture` is
transactional, so the flip is invisible to every other session and a hard abort rolls it back too.

### ⭐ Cody blocked the first design — it would have defeated Article 7 INVISIBLY

The override was to be consumed by stamping `preflight_override_log.consumed_at`. That table carries
`pol_no_update` and `pol_no_delete`. **A `postgres`-owned `SECURITY DEFINER` bypasses RLS, so the
UPDATE would have succeeded.** That is the whole trap: the policy would have been defeated by a
function that read as compliant, and the fixture would have gone green on it.

Consumption moved to an **INSERT on the consuming side**: `refill_commit_log.preflight_override_id`
names the grant that let the commit through, and a partial UNIQUE index makes a second spend
physically impossible. Both logs stay append-only and the audit chain reads forwards. → **RISK 100.**
⭐ **STANDING RULE: when an append-only log needs "consumed" state, put the state on the CONSUMER.**
📌 Corollary: **"the DEFINER can write it" is not evidence that it may** — RLS bypass by ownership is
the normal case for every canonical writer here, so the policy never stops you. The review does.

The fixture correction was **recorded in its own migration**, not edited silently, and seq 37 came
back **stronger**: it now pins the audit chain (which commit spent which grant) instead of a flag.
Three assertions were added with it, including a non-vacuity guard so two NULLs can never read as a
match — the S-48 / S-52 discipline applied pre-emptively this time.

### ⛔ `pronargdefaults` caught the first apply — RISK 101

`CREATE OR REPLACE public.commit_refill_plan(date,text,uuid[])` failed with **`42P13: cannot remove
parameter defaults from existing function`**. The live signature is `p_machine_ids uuid[] DEFAULT
NULL::uuid[]` and the replacement had dropped it — **the same class as the 13-day driver-confirm
outage**. Postgres caught it; nothing else would have. 📌 **A failed `apply_migration` leaves NOTHING
behind** — verified immediately: no column, no version row, `max(version)` unmoved. Confirms leg 49.

📌 An overload carrying defaulted `p_force`/`p_force_reason` (mirroring stitch) was **rejected as a
design** for the same reason: beside the existing 3-arg form it makes every 3-arg call ambiguous. The
**grant-then-commit split** dodges the overload entirely and is better audit besides — the override
becomes an explicitly authorised act rather than a parameter anyone can pass.

### ⛔ THE FINDING — the Phase-2 gate's evidence object was structurally vacuous

`public.v_shadow_vs_live_plan_v3` (built leg 12, registered, never questioned since) reads
`pod_refill_plan_shadow` FULL JOIN `pod_refill_plan`. But `pod_refill_plan_shadow` holds **0 rows**,
and **`position('pod_refill_plan_shadow' in prosrc) = 0`** on `engine_add_pod_v3` — the v3 engine's
**only** INSERT target is `pod_refills_shadow` (ADR §9 addendum: the sibling landed at P2, not P3.1,
precisely because the Phase-2 acceptance grain is `pod_refills`).

So the object nominated to carry "nightly diff vs v19" **could never return a row on any date**, and
its output would have read as **PARITY**. This is the S-48 / S-52 failure class sitting in the one
place where it would have been believed and acted on.

⭐ **It was found by probing the object's ROW COUNT on a date where both engines had just run — not
by reading its definition, which looks entirely reasonable.** VERIFY THEN ACT (LAW 13) again.

`golden.scratch` key `'truth'` and requires the views to reproduce every number. **No assertion

### ⛔ L51-U2 — the P2 regression run surfaced a real P2.1 defect (LAW 8: halt → bisect → fix → green)

P2 came back **9 fixtures / 294 pass / 1 fail**: **fixture 2 seq 8**, "I7: status ok implies a
non-NULL velocity", **0 → 2** between 09:51Z and 10:15Z. Bisected and **reproduced directly on the
base view with no fixture involved** ⇒ not a regression from L51-U1, which adds only views over
`pod_refills` / `pod_refills_shadow` / `blocked_demand`.

```sql
WHEN a.stock_hours < w.floor_hours THEN 'below_floor'   -- NULL < 48.0 → NULL, not TRUE
ELSE 'ok'                                                -- so NULL falls through to the optimistic default
```

`stock_hours` is NULL when a series was **never observed in stock** in the window. `velocity_instock`
guards with `>=` and correctly returns NULL; `velocity_status` guards with `<` and falls through to
`'ok'`. Status says healthy, no velocity behind it.

⭐ **THE GENERAL LESSON: the value guard and the status guard were written against the same column
with opposite NULL behaviour.** `>=` fails SAFE on NULL; `<` fails OPEN. Wherever a status column
classifies what a value column computes, the two predicates must agree on NULL **explicitly**.

📌 **A now()-anchored window makes an invariant intermittent.** `t_start = now() - 30 days` slides
continuously; the last usable observation fell out between the two runs. The fixture did not go
flaky — **it went TRUE**. An intermittent red whose object has a rolling window is a reason to FIX,
not to pin the assertion.

⭐ **Blast radius measured BEFORE applying.** `engine_add_pod_v3` reads `velocity_status` from the
**SHELF-grain `v_shelf_instock_velocity_split_v3`**, not this pod-grain view — and that sibling has
**0 violations across all 544 rows** (524 `ok`), because it anchors on
`max(weimi_device_status.snapshot_at)` rather than `now()`. It was deliberately **NOT** patched:
nothing to patch, and touching the engine's live input to fix a defect it does not have is scope
drift. v19 does not reference `velocity_status`; no other `public` view does. ⇒ **zero engine
impact, live or shadow.** 2 rows changed label.

Fixed to `stock_hours IS NULL OR stock_hours < floor_hours`. **`below_floor`, not a new status** —
NULL is zero observed in-stock hours, genuinely below the floor, and a fourth value would red
fixture 2's `status_other` assertion. Applied by anchored substitution that RAISES if the anchor
moved, if already guarded, or if the view has lost `security_invoker` (which had to be restated
explicitly: `CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW` with no `WITH` clause is not a safe way to inherit reloptions,
and losing it would silently widen read access). Violations **2 → 0**, domain unchanged,
`security_invoker=true` preserved, **fixture 2 back to 49/49**.

### ⛔ RISK 104 (NEW) — a dead leg leaves the DB and the docs AHEAD of the log, and `git status` stays silent

The handoff invariant is _"nothing half-applied"_, and it is enforced at **leg close**. A leg that
dies mid-flight never reaches its close, so the invariant is never applied — it leaves applied
migrations, a green fixture and an edited ADR with **no log entry, no registry rows and no migration
files**. Because the filing debt is what `git status` measures, the count matched the prediction
**exactly** and looked like health.

⭐ **THE MITIGATION, and it is cheap: `max(version)` is the load-bearing STEP R probe, not the doc
hashes.** A doc hash only fires if the dead leg happened to edit a doc — 52a did, which is luck. The
migration high-water mark fires unconditionally on any applied work. ⭐ **STANDING RULE: at STEP R,
compare `max(version)` and the `prd110%` count against the pointer BEFORE trusting any other claim,
and treat a forward gap as adoptable work to be verified and recorded — never as corruption to be
undone.** Re-running 52a's migrations would have been the destructive mistake here.

### ⭐ The finding that shaped the whole design: on a NORMAL night the engine REFUSES

`_assert_gate_zero` raises `check_violation` whenever machines are `picked` with `confirmed_at IS
NULL`. Under **LAW 11 Gate 0 is manual-only**, so that is not an edge case — it is the _ordinary_
state of every night between cron 13's 16:00Z pick and CS confirming. A runner that recorded it as
`error` would paint every ordinary night as a failure and **bury the real ones**.

⭐ So `blocked_gate0` is a first-class status, distinct from `error` and from `ok`. ⛔ **The runner
never auto-confirms** — that would be exactly the auto-fallback CS decision #1 forbids, and it is
the tempting "fix" precisely because it would make the logs look green. Fixture 37 seq 11-16 pin the
whole path: it must RETURN rather than propagate (seq 11), classify as `blocked_gate0` (seq 12),
leave a durable row carrying SQLSTATE **23514** (seq 13/14) and the human-readable reason (seq 15),
and write **no** shadow rows for that date (seq 16). Seq 15's captured message is the real one:
_"Gate 0 not passed: 1 machine(s) picked but unconfirmed for plan_date 2030-02-08."_

### ⭐ A dead schedule writes NOTHING, so the detector fires on ABSENCE

`v_shadow_runner_health_v3` cannot be a row-inspector: the failure mode under test produces a
**clean empty table**, which any row-inspecting check reads as health. `is_healthy` is anchored on
`log_rows > 0 AND last_run_at >= now() - 30h` and is explicitly **FALSE, never NULL**, on an empty
log (RISK 103 — `false AND NULL` = `false`). Proven with fixture 31's forced-rollback probe: the log
is emptied inside a subtransaction, the verdict is read into a PL/pgSQL variable, the rollback is
forced, and seq 19 confirms the table survived intact. Same lesson as PRD-109's INV-10 — **the
absence is the signal**.

📌 **`is_healthy` and `is_measuring` are two columns on purpose.** A long `blocked_gate0` streak is
alive and sterile: running perfectly, measuring nothing. One boolean would either cry wolf or hide a
fortnight of lost telemetry.

### The schedule — cron 45, `22 21 * * *`, derived rather than picked

⭐ **21:22 UTC = 01:22 Dubai, and the date arithmetic is the point.** `resolve_refill_plan_date()`
returns Dubai _today_ before 18:00, so at 01:22 it yields the **same plan_date cron 13 targeted** at
16:00Z (20:00 Dubai ⇒ tomorrow). Verified against the function body, not assumed. It also sits ~5 h
after the pick so CS has had time to clear Gate 0, and after crons 2 (19:59), 31 (20:30) and 5
