### ✅ L54-U1 ADOPTED AND VERIFIED — two real defects in leg 53's work, both now closed

Leg 53 closed clean by every check it ran. **It was still wrong twice**, and the dead leg caught
both. Recording the mechanism, because it generalises past these two objects:

**(1) S-58 (NEW) — a green fixture run is not an idempotent fixture.** Fixture 37 seq 13 counted
rows in `shadow_runner_log_v3`, which is **append-only and durable by design**. It was green only on
its virgin run; the count drifts 1 → 2 → 3. Leg 53 ran it once, saw 27/27, recorded that, and left a
`run_all('P2')` running that it could not read — that run returned **26/27**. ⛔ **This was a latent
STEP-7 failure already sitting in the suite**, since S7 requires `run_all()` ×3 to be identical.
⛔ The obvious fix — let the fixture DELETE its own rows — was **refused on Cody review**: the table
is an Article 7 append-only log with `tg_srl_v3_no_update` and an audit trigger, and a deleting
fixture would contradict **its own seq 19**, which exists to prove the absence probe left the log
intact. ✅ Re-expressed as a **DELTA bracketed across the gate0 call** — mutates nothing, idempotent
by construction, and **strictly stronger** than the original: it proves _this_ run wrote exactly one
row, where an absolute count could be satisfied by another writer's row. ⛔ Not weakened to `gte 1`;
a double-write is the regression it exists to catch.

**(2) S-57 was WIDER than leg 53 recorded — and the cause will recur on every new public table.**
Leg 53 wrote that `shadow_runner_log_v3` "deliberately follows the `pod_refills_shadow` standard".
Live grants said otherwise: it carried the **same** loose INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE/TRUNCATE for
`authenticated`. ⭐ **A `GRANT` is additive. Supabase default privileges have already granted ALL on
a new table in `public`, so `GRANT SELECT` adds nothing and narrows nothing — only an explicit
REVOKE narrows.** `pod_refills_shadow` is SELECT-only because something actually revoked.

**Re-probed live this leg, not taken from the migration:**

```
engine_forecast_error_v3  authenticated → SELECT   ✅
shadow_runner_log_v3      authenticated → SELECT   ✅
pod_refills_shadow        authenticated → SELECT   ✅ (the house standard, unchanged)
```

**⭐ The object CS's correction actually names is NOT the object to fix.** `v_pod_substitutes` is the
pure-Pearson view (`pearson > 0`, symmetric, no category, no stock, no exclusion) — but it has
**ZERO consumers in `pg_proc`**. It is dead code. ⛔ Fixing it would have changed nothing. The live

`rank_slot_suitability`.

**`find_substitutes_for_shelf` scored against CS's three rules — it satisfies exactly ONE:**

| CS rule (BUILD-SPEC line 89)                      | live v1                                                              |
| ------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| (1) SAME CATEGORY first                           | ⛔ **absent** — `product_category` appears nowhere in the body       |
| (2) exclude anything already on the machine       | ✅ **present** — the `present` CTE (slot_lifecycle ∪ live stock > 0) |
| (3) rank perf/margin/stock, Pearson tiebreak ONLY | ⛔ **inverted** — Pearson is the PRIMARY multiplier                  |

The score is `COALESCE(basket_corr, 0.05) * ln(1 + wh_stock)`, so a high-correlation **complement**
outranks any in-category peer. 📌 Rule (2) being already live is worth knowing: the BUILD SPEC calls
it "the documented in-machine-duplicate bug", but the live function does exclude. Do not re-fix it.

was right to fire.** Read its own description: _"Attributed by transaction, not by a global count
delta, so a concurrent live writer can neither cause a false red nor mask a real write."_
`run_all` is **transactional**, so _one call = one transaction_. Every prior leg ran
`run_all('P2')` **alone**. I ran `run_all('P0')`, `('P1')` and `('P2')` inside **one SQL statement**,
therefore inside **one transaction** — and **fixture 10 (P0) legitimately INSERTs into

synthetic dates**, so LAW 12 is respected — 9 live rows ≥ 2030-01-01 against 6,502 real ones).
Fixture 14's txn-scoped tripwire then attributed fixture 10's legal writes to fixture 14's run.

⛔ **The tripwire's transaction attribution silently assumes ONE PHASE PER TRANSACTION.** That
assumption held for 54 legs because nobody had ever combined phases in a single statement.

📌 **This matters for STEP 7, which is why it is being recorded and not just fixed.** S7 requires
`golden.run_all()` **×3 consecutive with identical results**. Anyone who "optimises" that by batching
phases into one statement will get a **false red on fixture 14 seq 91** and will spend a leg hunting
a live-plan-write that never happened. ⛔ **Run one phase per call. Always.**

double-allocation / phantom-mint class. v3 nets off `SUM(pod_refills.qty)` for the same pod and
plan_date and **names its allocation model in the output** rather than hiding it.

### ⭐ S-66 — THE GRAIN WAS NEVER THE DEFECT. THE PAIRING PREDICATE WAS.

"M2M SKU-level" reads like a re-graining job. It is not. Probed before writing anything:
`refill_dispatching` already carries `boonz_product_id`, `is_m2m`, `m2m_partner_id`, `m2m_transfer_id`,
and **all 36 live `is_m2m` rows carry a SKU — zero nulls.** So the storage was already right.

⛔ The defect is what the writer does with that column. Read from the body of
`convert_removes_to_m2m_transfer`, not inferred:

```
INSERT INTO refill_dispatching (... pod_product_id, boonz_product_id ...)
VALUES              (... v_row.pod_product_id, v_row.boonz_product_id ...)   -- SOURCE values, VERBATIM
```

No check that either value belongs on `p_dest_shelf_id`. Converting Removes off a `Krambals & Zigi`
shelf into a `Zigi` shelf mints destination rows carrying the **wrong pod** and **Krambals SKUs**.
⭐ Consequence for scope: the fix is a _validation_ unit — no DDL, no backfill, no re-grain.

### ⭐ THE ANCHOR SET — one source shelf, two destinations, mirror-image expected results

`MPMCC-1058-0000-R0` carries **both** a Krambals shelf (A05) and a Zigi shelf (A06). That made a much
stronger fixture possible than the spec's single case: feed the SAME 7-SKU / 14-unit mixed input at
both, and the two eligible sets must come out as exact complements.

```
SOURCE  VML-1004-0500-O1 A07 'Krambals & Zigi' — 7 Active SKUs (4 Krambals + 3 Zigi)

ANCHOR A  -> MPMCC-1058 A06 'Zigi'          ANCHOR B  -> MPMCC-1058 A05 'Krambals'
 eligible 3 Zigi SKUs (6u)                   eligible 4 Krambals SKUs (8u)
 headroom 15-6 = 9  -> no clamp fires        headroom 6-5 = 1  -> clamps HARD
 transfer 6 · return 8 · clamped 0           transfer 1 · return 13 · clamped 7
 PURE ELIGIBILITY CASE                       MIRROR + OVERFLOW CASE
```

required _on top of_ the status filter, not instead of it. Both guards are in the function and both
are pinned by the fixture (seq 9-17).

### ⛔ S-69 — THE CAPACITY MODEL HAS NO OBSERVATIONAL BASIS. `trip_events` IS EMPTY.

BUILD-SPEC line 93 asks for a "day capacity model (driver-hours, cluster travel, pack time)".
`trip_events` is the only table shaped to carry per-visit driver timings and it holds **0 rows**.
Nothing else in the schema observes minutes. The only live-calibrated capacity primitive is
`pick_urgency_params.driver_capacity = 8`, which the existing Gate-0 picker already respects — so
the VAR picker **reads it** rather than minting a second, divergeable copy.

"MODELLED, not measured", and `reasoning.day_capacity.cost_basis` repeating it on **every output
row**. ⛔ Nobody may present the selected list as a capacity FACT; it is an assumption with the
assumption printed on it.

M_CAD  NOVO-1023-0000-W0    0a9a4836   dsv 15 gap 4    VAR   7.82   CADENCE-DUE

A VAR-only picker would not select M_CAD. A cadence-only picker would not select M_TOP. Both must
appear with the reason that chose them (seq 33/34/35).

⭐ **The assertions pin IDENTITIES AND ORDERINGS, never AED constants.** VAR moved 549.37 → 545.75
between two probes twenty minutes apart, so a hardcoded number would red the suite within hours
for no defect. What cannot move without a real defect: that the function's figure equals an
independent recomputation from base tables (seq 27, **0 mismatches across all 31 machines**), that
the ordering obeys cadence-then-money (seq 31/32, 0 inversions), that capacity is respected
(37/38), and that unpriceable/unmeasurable shelves are counted rather than silently zeroed (43/44).

### ⭐ THE CODY REVIEW — APPROVED WITH ONE REVISION, AND IT WAS NOT THE QUESTION THAT WAS ASKED

Three explicit questions, submitted for a ruling rather than a stamp.
**(a) Article 14 not engaged** — the article's test is silent staleness in a materialized query
result; a single-row parameter table materializes nothing. P2.2 / P2.4 precedent stands.
**(c) advisory-only sufficient** — `STABLE` + `SECURITY INVOKER` means Postgres itself refuses the
write, so the fixture pins corroborate rather than enforce. A pick LIST is not a pick.

`v_machine_priority.urgency` (AED vs dimensionless; urgency has **no revenue term at any point**) —
now declared in METRICS_REGISTRY. But the function read `days_since_visit` from
`v_machine_priority`, which registry line 49 lists as a **consumer** of the visit clock; the owner
is `v_machine_health_signals`. Probed live: **31 machines, 0 disagreements** — numerically
identical, nothing broken. ⛔ Which is exactly why it was worth fixing: a copy that agrees is
indistinguishable from the original until the day it does not. Corrected, pinned by seq 54, and
seq 55 now forces every row to NAME the object it read.
⛔ **Standing condition carried forward:** the first consumer that turns this ranking into a
`machines_to_visit` row is a NEW class (b) Cody review.

### ⭐ S-75 — THE EXPIRY GUARD WAS GREEN AND BLOCKING NOTHING

The LAW-7 guard was written as `(expiry - plan_date) >= projected_days_to_sell`. The fixture
anchors on the synthetic **2030**-02-13 (LAW 12). Real expiry dates run 2026-08-26 → 2027-11-10 —
all before 2030 — so the guard silently collapsed into "keep only shelves whose expiry is NULL":

```
candidate pairs                       802
admitted by the 2030 guard             52   <- exactly the pairs with UNKNOWN expiry
admitted judged from the real world   765
BLOCKED judged from the real world     37   <- the rule actually doing its job
```

⛔ Nothing errors. The assertion would have gone GREEN over a degenerate population. ⭐ **Same
disease as S-70 wearing a calendar instead of a NULL.** Fixed by measuring the horizon from
`CURRENT_DATE` (also correct in production: `p_plan_date` is a batch key, not the moment stock
moves), and by adding **seq 19 — a sensor FOR the sensor**, which reds if the expiry-blocked set
ever empties.

### ⛔ S-76 — THE DRY-RUN SMOKE TEST PROVED NOTHING, BECAUSE `p_dry_run` SKIPS THE INSERT

The pre-apply check called the function with `p_dry_run => true`. It returned 25 correct rows and
read as proof. It had **never executed the write path**, which failed on every real call with
`42702: column reference "plan_date" is ambiguous` — the `ON CONFLICT` inference list cannot be
disambiguated from the identically-named `RETURNS TABLE` OUT parameters. Fixed by naming the
constraint (`ON CONFLICT ON CONSTRAINT rp_v3_unique_heartbeat`).
⭐ **What caught it was fixture 43's S-70 wrappers.** The aborted scenario rolled back and left the
PREVIOUS run's scratch in place, so the assertions were reading stale data from an older run.
Unwrapped "count the violations, expect 0" assertions would have found no `out` row, counted 0 and
reported PASS on a function erroring on every call. **S-70 paid for itself one leg after being
written down.**

### ⭐ THE CODY REVIEW — approved with revisions, and it found the unreachable status

**(a) Article 14 not engaged**: `status`/`reviewed_by`/`reviewed_at` are state no view can derive,
so a proposal queue is not a materialization. ⛔ But Cody named the real exposure the question had
missed: `fit_score` and `projected_days_to_sell` genuinely ARE materialized query results that
decay as velocity moves — visible only because `proposed_at` stamps every row.
**(b) Article 5**: the FE cannot flip status (SELECT-only grant, no UPDATE policy), which
satisfies the article — but a CHECK sees only the NEW row, so it enforces the _vocabulary_, never
the _transition graph_. ⛔ **`'expired'` is reserved and no writer produces it** — a status value
the schema promises and cannot deliver, and the very mechanism that would have bounded the
staleness in (a). Both documented in the DDL rather than quietly left.
**(c)** Leaving the three broken functions is correct for this migration; the anon grant is filed
as its own unit.

### ⛔ S-85 — a 38/38 GREEN fixture guarded a function that threw on its HAPPIEST path

```
ERROR: 55000 record "v_sub" is not assigned yet
DETAIL: The tuple structure of a not-yet-assigned record is indeterminate.
CONTEXT: PL/pgSQL assignment "v_ladder := jsonb_build_array(...)"
```

For its entire P3.1b life `resolve_supply_ladder_v3` raised on **every call whose demand was
satisfiable from the primary warehouse**. The rung-2 **log** entry dereferences `v_sub` at two
places unconditionally; the `SELECT INTO` that assigns it runs **only when rung 1 has already
FAILED**. ⛔ A `CASE` guard cannot prevent this — PL/pgSQL must resolve a record's tuple structure
to build the expression, whichever branch executes.

⭐ **Why fixture 40 could not see it, and why that is the transferable lesson.** Anchors A and B are
**both deliberately starved**: A is the sentinel trap (Fade Fit, zero real stock), B is the
contention case (Vitamin Well, gross stock fully claimed). Between them they proved rungs 2-6 and
**never once executed terminal rung 1**. The fixture was a faithful record of the 07-30 incident
and, for exactly that reason, a systematically incomplete test of the function.
⛔ **A fixture built from an incident inherits the incident's blind spot.**

**Cody review (LAW 3) — ⚠️ APPROVE WITH REVISIONS**, articles 2/4/12/13/14/16. Classification
**(c) read-only**; already `SECURITY INVOKER` + `STABLE`, so "writes nothing" is a Postgres
guarantee. Article 12 ✅ true `CREATE OR REPLACE` — `pronargdefaults` pinned at **1** before and
after (RISK 101), identity args / volatility / security mode / `search_path` / `proacl` all
byte-identical, so no overload was minted. **The revision was not SQL:** mandatory correction of
`RPC_REGISTRY.md:1066`, which described an object that threw on its most common input — the same
failure class as S-81. Done before close. Cody also raised a **pre-existing Article 16 finding, not
introduced here and explicitly not fixed in this unit**: rung 4 reads
`COALESCE(v_shelf_state.velocity_instock, velocity_raw, 0)`, and per S-73 `velocity_instock` is NULL
on all 656 shelves, so rung 4 silently runs on `velocity_raw` while appearing to prefer in-stock
velocity. Now named in the registry rather than silently inherited.

**Two migrations, both dry-run as `BEGIN; …; ROLLBACK;` first, both applied, both filed to disk at
their REGISTERED versions:**

| version          | name                                          | what                                                                                   |

### THE UNIT — `stitch_v3` skeleton, and the three defects found building it

Reconnaissance confirmed S-62: no `stitch_v3`. The pipeline is `pod_refills` → approve →
`pod_refill_plan` → `stitch_pod_to_boonz` → `refill_plan_output`, so stitch's job is pod → **boonz
SKU** — and no SKU-grain shadow existed. ADR §2 pre-authorizes a sibling "on identical terms", so
`refill_plan_output_shadow` was created under it.

⛔ **`record_blocked_demand_v3` hard-refuses any source but `'engine_add'`** ("stitch and pack
writers land in Phase 3/4"), and its gap source `_blocked_demand_gaps_v3` reads **live**
`pod_refills`, not the shadow. So shadow runs do not write live `blocked_demand` — established
precedent, matched here: shortfalls are carried in the shadow ledger, and the live `source='stitch'`
writer lands with the cutover.

⭐ **Conservation by construction, not by guard** (the S-85 lesson applied rather than quoted).
Placeable rows accumulate into `v_placed`; blocked is then `qty_needed - v_placed` — **never** the
ladder's `qty_shortfall`. Any rung that places less than asked lands the remainder automatically,
and the total is asserted before return.

**Three defects the build surfaced, in the order they were caught:**

⛔ **S-90 — plpgsql does not validate SQL inside function bodies at CREATE time.** The first
`stitch_v3` referenced `shelf_configurations.pod_product_id`, **a column that does not exist**. It
compiled cleanly, and both dry-runs passed because neither entered the m2m branch. Fixed to read
`v_shelf_state`, the P1.2 canonical shelf↔pod object. ⛔ **A clean CREATE plus a green happy-path
dry-run prove nothing about a branch they did not enter.**

⛔ **Cody revision (LAW 3) — ⚠️ APPROVE WITH REVISIONS**, articles 1/2/3/4/6/7/8/12/14/16. Article
14 ✅ (ADR §2 sibling; §3's argument transfers). Article 1 ✅ (`stitch_v3` is the sole writer and its
only INSERTs target that table). Article 4 ✅ (`app.via_rpc`/`app.rpc_name`, NULL and source-run
validation, role gate). **Article 7 ⚠️:** the table advertised ledger semantics enforced by RLS —
but `USING (false)` does **not** bind the owner, `service_role`, or a `SECURITY DEFINER` body,
which is exactly how `stitch_v3` writes. Replaced with a `BEFORE UPDATE OR DELETE` trigger
mirroring `tg_pod_refills_shadow_append_only`; UPDATE and DELETE then both measured **refused
42501** on the owner path before apply.

⛔ **S-88 — RLS IS NOT A WRITE GUARD; THE GRANT IS.** Fixture 44 seq 25 was a routine Article-1
check against the table this leg created — **and it failed on the first run**. `ALTER DEFAULT
PRIVILEGES` grants the `authenticated` role everything at CREATE time; `REVOKE ALL … FROM PUBLIC`
does not touch a role grant and `GRANT` only adds. ⛔ **And TRUNCATE bypasses RLS _and_ every
`FOR EACH ROW` trigger** — so the "immutable ledger" was erasable in one statement by any logged-in
user. The sweep was then **closed, not sampled** (S-79) and found the identical hole on **seven
siblings**: `inventory_events` (append-only event log, Article 7), `product_sourcing`,
`blocked_demand`, `machines_to_visit` (the Gate-0 table, 1,240 rows), `shelf_composition`,
`inventory_anomalies`, `demand_calendar`. Revoked **TRUNCATE only** — INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE left as
found since RLS gates them and revoking could break an FE path; probed first, **0 functions and 0
crons** issue TRUNCATE against any of the eight.

### ⛔ S-94 — TWO OBJECTS CAN DISAGREE ABOUT "AVAILABLE" AND BOTH BE RIGHT

`resolve_supply_ladder_v3` counts supply via `v_wh_pickable` (expiry vs **today**);
`wh_fefo_for_line` filters `expiration_date >= p_plan_date`. On production dates they differ by one
day and the stricter one is **correct**. On a synthetic 2030 fixture date they diverge **totally** —
the newest real non-sentinel batch expires **2027-12-29**, so the ladder rules units placeable that
FEFO can bind none of. ⭐ Resolved by naming an AUTHORITY SPLIT rather than reconciling: the **ladder
owns how many**, the **seam owns which SKU**, and the residue ships as `qty_unbound` with a named
reason (LAW 5 in the identity dimension). ⛔ The fixture consequence is the real lesson — a fixture
running only on its own 2030 date would have gone green while proving **nothing but the refusal**.
Fixture 46 therefore calls the seam on **both** horizons.

### The incident P3.1e closes

BUILD SPEC P0.5 names **three** writers of the ledger — `engine_add_pod`, `stitch`, and the FEFO-bind
step. Only `engine_add` existed (cron 43, nightly since P0.5). Every unit `stitch_v3` stranded since
P3.1c carried `blocked_demand_promotion = 'source=stitch writer lands with the live cutover (P3.1e)'`
and **reached no human**: the plan knew the demand was unmet and procurement was never told. Stitch
and the FEFO-bind step are ONE source, not two — after P3.1d the binding happens inside `stitch_v3`
and its unbound rows land in the same shadow output.

### ⭐ The real work was a mapping decision, not plumbing

`blocked_demand.reason` is a four-value CHECK; stitch computes seventeen rich named reasons. The map
is **lossy by design**, organised by the action a human must take — `blocked_no_wh` BUY it ·
`partial_wh_limited` BUY the balance · `routing_gap` MOVE it · `substitution_exhausted` DECIDE — and
the loss is compensated: the original named reason always rides into `reasoning->'components'`.
⭐ It lives in its OWN function (`_blocked_demand_reason_map_v3`) so it is testable without a
pipeline run. That mattered: on this fleet the ladder stops at rung 1 or 2, so an end-to-end fixture
can only exercise **2 of the 17** named reasons. The other fifteen are asserted directly.

### ⛔ Two row kinds, one ledger row — forced by the schema, made honest in the payload

`uq_blocked_demand_open` keys on `(plan_date, machine, shelf, pod, source)`, so a shelf gets one open
row per source. That merges **`unplaced`** (an explicit `Blocked` row) with **`unbound`** (a row that
DOES ship at qty>0 but which no batch could name a SKU for). Both are demand no nameable batch can
serve, so `qty_blocked` is their SUM, and `qty_unplaced`/`qty_unbound`/`components[]` split it back
out. ⛔ Keyed on **`anchor_pod_product_id`**: a rung-2 substitution emits against the SUBSTITUTE pod
while the `Blocked` row carries the ANCHOR, and keying on the emitted pod would split one shelf's
demand into two rows that each look like a separate problem. Fixture 47 assertions 14/15/16/17 pin it.

### ⛔ S-96 — A BAD LAST STATEMENT ROLLS BACK THE FIXTURE RUNS IN ITS BATCH

S-95's second face. The runner sends a file as ONE implicit transaction, so a syntax error in the
FINAL statement discards the `run_fixture()` calls before it. Fixtures 5 and 105 were "run", the
reader threw, and `golden.runs` still showed runs from **12:55** — six hours stale — which reads as
green. ⭐ Caught by checking `started_at` against the wall clock. Habit: `run_fixture` calls are the
ONLY statements in their batch; read `golden.runs` separately. 📌 The reader bug is its own lesson:
`golden.runs.detail` is a **jsonb** array, not a PG array (S-65 reads ambiguously) — `unnest()` fails,
use `jsonb_array_elements(...) AS t(e)`. There is no `n_skip` column.

feeds it `m2mXnot_an_m2m_reason` and requires the safe default.

### The incident P3.4 closes — and it is one this leg CREATED AND CAUGHT, not one from the field

BUILD SPEC P3.4 is a single line ("revenue/facing/day report + proposal queue"), so the fixture-first
question was what the incident even IS. It turned out to be the construction itself. ⛔ **MEASURED, NOT
REASONED:** the obvious build — group `v_shelf_instock_velocity_split_v3` by its emitted
`pod_product_id` — is WRONG. That view canonicalises the Hunter/Hunter Ridge alias INTERNALLY (S-37)
but emits the RAW pod key per shelf, while `pod_shelf_count` and `velocity_*_pod` are FAMILY-level.
Grouping on the emitted key splits one 2-lane family into TWO rows that EACH claim `facings = 2` and
EACH claim the full family velocity, with only their own shelf's stock. On the 7 dual-Hunter machines
that doubles attributed revenue and would emit **two** "drop a lane" proposals for a family that
should lose one. I built that version first and saw it in the output before writing any DDL.

### ⭐ The fix was to READ IDENTITY FROM ITS OWNER, not to write another copy of the alias rule

`v_shelf_sales_identity` IS the canonical alias object (METRICS_REGISTRY line 44: _"Any future
per-product velocity read must use this object, not re-aggregate sales_history"_), it is already
collapsed to one row per merged family, and — the find of the leg — **it already carries `facings`,
`stock`, `cap` and a calendar `dvel` at exactly that grain.** Verified live: **525** rows,
`(machine_id, pod_product_id)` UNIQUE (0 duplicate keys), and its `facings` agrees with the velocity
view's `pod_shelf_count` on **every** family where both exist. So the report takes identity + facings +
stock + cap + calendar velocity from it, and ONLY the in-stock rate from the split view. This ADDS a
consumer to the canonical object, which is the direction **S-38** (converge the alias copies) wants —
it does not add an eighth copy.

### ⛔ THE PRD-108 ppad TRAP, FOUND IN A NEW OBJECT — and turned into the feature

The pointer warned against building a facings/day metric on `rank_slot_suitability.proven` (units per
SELLING day, ~23.6x overstated). This unit never touches that column — but `velocity_instock_pod` is
the **same class of quantity**: sales ÷ in-stock hours, i.e. a per-IN-STOCK-day rate. **Measured across
456 live families: it is ≥ the calendar rate on every single one (min ratio 1.006), mean 1.121x, MAX
14.003x, with 20 families overstated by >50%.** Silently dividing that by facings would inflate a
lane's apparent earnings up to 14x on exactly the shelves that run dry. ⭐ So BOTH are exposed and
neither is "the" velocity: `rev_per_facing_day_realized` (calendar — what the lane earned) beside
`rev_per_facing_day_potential` (in-stock — what it earns while stocked), with `starvation_ratio` their
quotient. **That ratio is not a nuisance to correct away; it is the only admissible evidence for
ADDING a lane** — high revenue per lane alone argues for restocking it, not for building a second one.
`dvel` confirmed arithmetically as calendar (`units_30d/30`: 5/30 = 0.167, 24/30 = 0.800 on live rows).

### ⛔ S-98 (NEW, and it cost this leg its second half) — A CLIENT-SIDE TIMEOUT DOES NOT END THE TRANSACTION

The first draft of `propose_facing_changes_v3` computed its five skip counters as six separate
subqueries over `v_facing_performance_v3`. That view inherits the ~20 s cost of
`v_shelf_instock_velocity_split_v3`, so the call was **seven full evaluations** and blew the 2-minute
Bash timeout. ⛔ **The client gave up; the transaction did not.** The dry-run was
`BEGIN; CREATE TABLE …; CREATE FUNCTION …; SELECT propose(…); ROLLBACK;` — when the client died the
`ROLLBACK` never arrived, so an open transaction sat holding its DDL locks. Every subsequent
connection — `psql` script AND MCP alike, down to `SELECT 1` — then failed with _"Connection
terminated due to connection timeout"_ for **~3 minutes**, and the postgres log shows the mechanism
exactly: `process 1238 still waiting for AccessShareLock on relation 17343` at 19:49:51, 19:50:00 and
19:50:52, with `canceling statement due to statement timeout` at 19:50:10. It cleared on its own
(recovery confirmed by poll at ~160 s; `pg_locks` ungranted now **0**).

⚠️ **A correction worth recording, because it nearly became a false incident report.** Mid-diagnosis I
read "no log events after 19:50:52" as "the DB has been stalled for twenty minutes". It had not been:
`get_logs` returns a bounded snapshot window, and its newest row is not the current time. ⛔ **Never
infer liveness from the absence of rows in a log page** — probe the DB.

The registry had already written the rule I broke: **S-26 / RISK 88, "any consumer must read it ONCE
per run and join; machine-scoping does NOT reduce the cost because the inner `vel` CTE is
MATERIALIZED."** ⭐ The fix is in the staged file: materialise the view into ONE

### ⛔ THE DEFECT THE DRY RUN CAUGHT — `ON COMMIT DROP` IS NOT `ON RETURN DROP` (S-101)

The staged proposer memoised the expensive view into `CREATE TEMP TABLE _fac_perf ON COMMIT DROP`.
That drops at **COMMIT**, not at RETURN — so a **second call inside one transaction** dies on
`relation "_fac_perf" already exists`. Calling it twice in one transaction is exactly what the
idempotency contract (STEP 7 S4) and fixture 48 (three calls) do. **The DDL-only dry run passed in
2 s; the BEHAVIOUR dry run failed immediately.** Fixed with two `DROP TABLE IF EXISTS pg_temp.…` lines
so scratch is rebuilt per call. ⭐ This is the concrete payoff of "dry-run the BEHAVIOUR, on a date
where it can actually FAIL", and of designing the fixture to call the engine three times.

Re-dry-run (DO-block + RAISE so the SERVER ends the transaction — S-98), all rolled back:
`dry3.written=3 dry=t rows_after_dry=0 | real.written=23 shrink=11 expand=12 considered=525 skipU=71
skipP=56 skipPrice=21 skipVel=76 skipThin=71 | pending=23 | rerun.written=0 rows_final=23`.

### ⛔ TWO FIXTURE CORRECTIONS, BOTH FOUND BY RUNNING IT

1. **Seq 44 was stricter than the ratified convention, and the ENGINE was right (S-104).** It demanded
   the proposer be non-executable by `authenticated`. Measured live, **all six** v3 engine objects
   carry the identical ACL `postgres=X | authenticated=X | service_role=X` — including the Cody-
   ratified sibling `propose_rotations_v3` and the S-81-hardened var picker. RPC_REGISTRY names this
   the house pattern. ⛔ The S-88 line is **anon** (seq 43, green), not authenticated. Revoking would
   have made one object inconsistent with six peers and changed a fleet convention — a CS decision,
   not a mid-loop edit. Seq 44 re-expressed as the stronger, self-maintaining invariant: **same ACL as
   the ratified sibling**, so a future CS tightening is followed automatically.
2. **Runtime, and a corrected reading of RISK 89 (S-102).** Fixture 48 made FOUR view reads and ran
   126 s, past the ~105 s gateway ceiling that fixtures 42/43 already sit at. The gateway returned a
   **524 — but the run had COMMITTED**: `golden.runs` held the full 51/1 verdict and the 23 proposals
   were in the table. ⛔ RISK 89's "on a 524 the query is already dead" is **false**; probe before
   concluding. Health was clean (0 ungranted locks, 0 idle-in-transaction) so this was not an S-98
   stuck transaction either. Fix: the dry-run/limit contract split into **fixture 49** (one call,
   34 s), leaving 48 at three reads. Seq 31/32/33 were **deleted rather than orphaned** — three
   assertions permanently red against scratch keys nothing writes is worse than no assertion.
   Also fixed **seq 44's `expect`**, which still read `'false'` from the superseded formulation and so
   reported a correct engine as a failure (**S-103**: an assertion edit is TWO fields, always).

### The overlay rule

**hard** — the human's number wins permanently for that plan_date; no engine re-run can move it.
**soft** — the human's number wins only while the engine still believes what it believed WHEN THE
EDIT WAS MADE; if the base moved since, the newer information wins and the edit **yields**, counted
and named. Neither lock may DROP an edit: `applied + yielded = considered`, asserted in the composer.
⭐ This is why `base_qty_at_edit` exists — an event must record what it was reacting to, or "has the
base moved?" is unanswerable. ⛔ `edits_considered` is counted **independently** of the loops that
consume it, so a duplicated base row RAISEs instead of being absorbed by an in-loop counter.

### The unit: P3.7, fixture first

**Reconnaissance turned the pointer's inherited obligation into a real defect.** Leg 70 flagged the
`compose → stitch` coupling as implicit and "probably the desired pipeline". It is neither.
`stitch_v3` with a NULL source resolves `ORDER BY produced_at DESC, run_id DESC`, and
`pod_refills_shadow.produced_at` DEFAULTs to `now()` — the **transaction** timestamp. A base run and
the run composed from it inside one transaction TIE, and the tie-break is uuid ordering of `run_id`.
⛔ **Whether a human's edits reached the stitched plan was a coin flip** (S-110). It read as working
only because every prior observation had composed in a later transaction than its base.

**Fixture 51 (plan_date 2030-02-21) landed BEFORE the engine (LAW 1)** and forces that coin flip to
its wrong face: the base run is minted with `run_id` = `ffffffff-ffff-4fff-bfff-…`, which sorts above
every random v4 uuid. With a composed run sitting on the same date, the implicit pick returns
`engine_add_pod_v3` and `implicit_equals_planned` is **false** — the pre-P3.7 path, measured,
discarding every edit silently.

⛔ **The RED baseline read 5/53 and THREE were vacuous, in two different shapes.** Two were the
familiar kind (green because nothing existed). The third was new: **seq 42 used `ne` against the
`no_pipeline` sentinel, and `'no_pipeline' <> 'none'` is TRUE** — a sentinel defeats `eq` but FEEDS
`ne` (S-111). Re-baselined at **3/53**, and the only three greens are the live-state tripwires that
must stay green at every moment of the build.

### What was built

`pipeline_runs_v3` (append-only receipt), `v_pipeline_runs_v3`, `run_pipeline_v3` and
`approve_pipeline_run_v3`. The pipeline passes **every run id explicitly** and re-asserts afterwards
that `stitch.source_run_id` is the run it planned, RAISEing rather than reporting a plan it did not
produce. ⭐ It **always** composes, even with zero edits: one pipeline means one shape, so "which run
did stitch consume?" stops having two possible answers. ⛔ A composed plan with zero lines does NOT
fall back to the base — that would resurrect every dropped line, the exact silent revert P3.6 exists
to prevent; it stops at `composed_empty`. ⛔ `p_promote_blocked` defaults **false**: D-29 stays parked.

**Single approve vocabulary.** At most one approval STANDS per `plan_date`, enforced by a partial
unique index rather than writer discipline. Approving a different run for a date that already has one
**retires the incumbent by name** — a late edit must stay approvable, but two approved plans for one
night must not exist. ⛔ S-105's order lesson applies again: retire the incumbent FIRST, or the
partial unique index rejects the claim every time.

### Cody review (LAW 3) — ⚠️ Approve with revisions, one required action, done before apply

### The RED was an ABSENCE, and the pointer's guess was right for the wrong reason

Leg 76 asked whether _any verb today re-offers a freed allocation at all_. The answer, probed rather
than assumed: **none does, and none ever did.** A sweep of every `propose_*` / `realloc*` / `release*`
function in `public` returns facings, rotations, decommission, rebalance, batch-dissolution and
pod-inventory-add — and **nothing whatsoever for freed allocation**. The mechanism sits in
`compose_plan_with_edits_v3`: a `drop` sets the effective qty to 0 and the line is simply **not
inserted**. The warehouse units it had claimed stop being claimed with no record that they came back.

That is the whole incident. On 2026-07-30 two AMZ machines were dropped post-draft while VML-1004
**A05** sat `blocked_no_wh` on Nutella Biscuits T12 — the very product AMZ-1029 **A06** had just
released 6 units of. Both shelves are real and both still carry that pod today; the fixture is built
on them, not on synthetic stand-ins.

### What shipped (2 migrations, one atomic unit)

1. `20260731234420` **fixture 11 first and RED** (LAW 1): 39 assertions, **22 pass / 17 fail**,
   recorded in `golden.runs` before a line of fix was written. ⭐ Every premise, freed-unit,
   boundary, conservation and tripwire assertion passed in that RED run — **all 17 reds were
   precisely the absent re-offer machinery**, which is what makes the baseline trustworthy.
2. `20260731234438` **`reallocation_proposals_v3`** (new CS-gated queue, RLS on, SELECT-only to
   `authenticated`, no anon grant) + **`propose_reallocations_v3(date,uuid,uuid,boolean)`**.
   ⭐ **Purely additive — not one existing engine was touched**, so no md5 pin moved and S-122
   never fired. All 15 engine md5s re-probed byte-identical after apply.

**Cody: ⚠️ approve-with-revisions (Articles 1/2/3/4/8/12/14/16). All three revisions were real and
were applied before apply** — the third one mattered most: the accounting guard compared a **pair**
count to a **source** count, so one source split across two claimants scored 2 and could have masked
a source represented nowhere. That is exactly the LAW-5 failure the function exists to prevent.

### Evidence

Fixture 11 **39/39** live. The queue holds 4 rows for the fixture date: the **VW 6u case matched**
(6 Nutella, AMZ-1029 A06 → VML-1004 A05, `status='proposed'`, unreviewed) and **3 `unclaimed`** rows
carrying the 4+3 Dubai Popcorn and 5 Chocolate Bar that nothing in the plan could use — recorded
rather than absorbed. Regression, each in its own transaction: **50 49/49 · 51 53/53**.
`machines_to_visit` **1240** and `v_blocked_demand_open` **20** provably unmoved,
`refill_plan_output` on the 2030 date **0** (LAW 4/12). 0 protected-entity writes, 0 rows deleted,
0 flags flipped, 0 cron schedules changed.

**Parked added:** ⏸️ **S-123** — the verb is built and proven but **NOT wired into `run_pipeline_v3`**;
wiring it edits an engine, moves `d16df04a`, and needs its own fixture first.

### ⛔ CODY'S TWO SUBSTANTIVE FINDINGS — both real, both would have shipped silently

**Verdict ⚠️ approve-with-revisions. Five revisions, three cosmetic, two that mattered:**

1. ⭐ **THE PROVENANCE INVARIANT WAS INERT.** Dara wrote
   `feedback_ids uuid[] NOT NULL CHECK (array_length(feedback_ids,1) >= 1)` to enforce "a proposal
   with no evidence is not a proposal". ⛔ **`array_length('{}',1)` returns NULL, and a CHECK
   constraint that evaluates to NULL PASSES.** The constraint admitted precisely the row it was
   written to forbid. Both `chk_fpr_v3_evidence` and `chk_pin_v3_provenance` carried it. Fixed with
   `cardinality()`. **This is the fixture-16 chain, so it is not a style note.**
2. ⭐ **THE UNIQUENESS INDEX WOULD HAVE TOMBSTONED ITS OWN SLOT.**
   `ux_pin_v3_active_one_per_kind` is partial on `revoked_at IS NULL` - but an **expired** pin is not
   revoked. A lapsed `until`-mode pin would hold its slot forever and could never be renewed. ⛔ **The
   predicate cannot simply be widened: index predicates must be IMMUTABLE and `now()` is not.**
   Resolved by materialising expiry as a revocation with a **system actor**
   (`revoke_reason='expired_system'`, `revoked_by IS NULL`), admitted as its own branch of
   `chk_pin_v3_revoke`. ⚠️ **Fixture 17 uses perpetual mode and would never have caught this** - the
   first `until` pin to lapse would have.

Plus: `security_invoker=true` on the view (ADR §7); `anon`/`PUBLIC`/`authenticated` **REVOKED** on all
four objects **before** `GRANT SELECT`, because ⛔ **a GRANT is additive and cannot narrow** (ADR
§11.2), with the privileges **read back naming `authenticated`** (§11.3); and `'superseded'` exempted
from the reviewer check, since supersede is a system action with no human in it.

⭐ **Article 14: NO ADR, and that is the considered answer.** These tables hold state no view can
derive - the same class as `rotation_proposals_v3` / `facing_proposals_v3` /
`reallocation_proposals_v3`, none of which needed one. The corrected test is **silent staleness**, not
table count (S-03). ⛔ **Dara's own handoff checklist asked for an ADR; that was the OLD misreading of
Article 14 and it was overruled at review.**

### ⭐ THE CONTRADICTION GUARD IS DDL, NOT A TRIGGER

`always_stock` and `never_stock` on one target are incoherent. Rather than a trigger (racy under
concurrency - two sessions each see no conflict and both commit - and droppable), **both kinds share
ONE partial-unique bucket**, so the incoherent pair raises 23505 and is **physically
unrepresentable**. ⭐ **Prefer DDL that cannot be bypassed over plpgsql that must be trusted.**

Leg 79 shipped the P4.1/P4.2 schema **deliberately inert**: `authenticated` held SELECT only and no
RPC wrote the three tables, so only `postgres`/`service_role` could put a row in them. This unit is
the other half.

40 assertions. ⭐ **It ran RED at 4 pass / 37 fail against functions that did not exist yet**, which

fail first_.

**Migration `20260801012431_prd110_p41_feedback_verbs`** — the three `SECURITY DEFINER` verbs.
Fixture 56 then ran **40/40**, and **40/40 again on a second run in its own transaction** (59 ms,

### What was actually decided, as opposed to typed

⭐ **THE PIN'S TARGET IS DERIVED FROM ITS EVIDENCE, NOT PASSED IN.** `propose_pin_from_feedback_v3`
takes feedback ids and the _shape_ of a pin; `machine_id`, `shelf_id` and `boonz_product_id` are read
off the cited rows. ⛔ **This is the difference between provenance that is load-bearing and
provenance that is decorative.** With the target as a parameter, `feedback_ids` is a comment — a
caller can cite a complaint about Oreo and pin Coke Zero, and every downstream assertion about "the
chain is intact" is satisfied by a chain that connects nothing. Derived, the mis-aim is
unrepresentable. Fixture 56 seq 9 asserts it as a `NOT EXISTS` over **all** proposals, not a spot
check on one.

⛔ **`count(DISTINCT)` IGNORES NULLS**, so "one product plus two product-less rows" would have read as
agreement and produced a pin from evidence that never named a product. The verb tallies the NULLs
separately. ⭐ **Same family as S-126** (`array_length` on an empty array is NULL): the aggregate that
_looks_ like it is checking something is the one to distrust.

⛔ **EVIDENCE IS SPENT ON CITATION** (`open` → `proposed`). Without it, one complaint justifies any
number of pins and P4.3's acceptance-rate telemetry would be counting the same row over and over —
a metric that improves as it degrades.

⭐ **THE DRIVER CHANNEL WRAPS, IT DOES NOT RESTATE.** `driver_propose_adjustment` already writes
`driver_recommendations`, `driver_feedback` and `refill_edit_signals`; restating those writes would
give one event two independent records that drift from their first divergence.
`chk_fbl_v3_driver_channel` is an **equivalence**, so the DDL forbids both a driver row without a rec
and a non-driver row with one — the wrap is not a convention, it is a constraint.

⛔ **AND THE WRAP RESTORES `app.rpc_name`.** The inner verb stamps the GUC with its own name, and
both settings are transaction-local. Without the restore, **every driver submission — and anything
writing later in the same transaction — is audited as `driver_propose_adjustment`.** ⭐ **This is the
class of defect that no amount of reading catches and one falsification run catches instantly.**

⛔ **THE CONTRADICTION GUARD READS THE BASE TABLE, NOT THE CANONICAL VIEW — AND THAT IS THE CORRECT
ANSWER, NOT A SHORTCUT.** `ux_pin_v3_stock_policy_exclusive` is partial on `revoked_at IS NULL`
**alone**; `v_planning_pins_active_v3` also hides _expired_ pins, which still occupy the slot. Read
the view and an expired-but-unrevoked `never_stock` slips past the guard and surfaces to CS as a bare
`23505`. ⭐ **The general rule, now written into `METRICS_REGISTRY.md` as an Article 16 carve-out: a
guard must be expressed over the SAME predicate as the constraint it protects.** "Is it in force?"
and "does it occupy the slot?" sound like one question and are two.

### The falsification — one targeted red, not a green run

⭐ **The fixture had already earned trust by starting red, but its subtlest claim was falsified
separately anyway.** Removing the two `set_config` lines that restore `app.rpc_name` produced
**exactly one red: seq 24, `got=driver_propose_adjustment`, `expect=submit_feedback_v3`.** Not two,
not a cascade — one, at precisely the assertion written for it. ⭐ **A falsification that produces a
_targeted_ red proves the assertion; a falsification that reddens half the suite proves only that
something broke.**

⭐ **Three defects were designed out before apply rather than discovered after**, in the leg-79
tradition: `min(uuid)` is not available on every server version (replaced with
`(array_agg(DISTINCT …))[1]`); the NULL-blind `count(DISTINCT)` above; and
`chk_pin_v3_revoke` demanding a named revoker, which means a supersede with no identified caller must
be **refused** rather than laundered as `expired_system` (Article 8).

## ✅ UNIT 1 (the leg's whole shipment) — `engine_add_pod_v3` READS PINS AS CONSTRAINTS

Migration **`20260801022432_prd110_p42_engine_pin_consumption`**. md5 `a79bbe1f` → **`e9f3caff`**.

and 19/6. **P4 is now 4 fixtures / 122 assertions.**

⭐ **THE MIGRATION WAS GENERATED, NOT TRANSCRIBED.** 592 lines of engine hand-copied into a migration
is a transcription bug waiting to happen. Instead: pull `pg_get_functiondef()`, apply four named
substitutions in Python with `assert count == 1` on each anchor, and re-check the generated source
against the two properties the fixture itself will test. ⛔ **`pg_get_functiondef()` returns NO
trailing semicolon** — the first dry run died with `syntax error at or near "DO"` 700 lines later,
which is a genuinely confusing way to learn it.

### What was decided, as opposed to typed

⛔ **`always_stock` IS A FLOOR ON UNITS, NOT ON DEPTH — and the fixture's own anchor forced it.**
The intuitive reading ("make sure at least 1 is on the shelf") is `GREATEST(1 - stock, 0)`. Fixture
16's A07 holds **stock 5**, so that reading yields 0 and seq 14 (`need_z > 0`) fails. It is worse
than wrong, it is _redundant_: as a depth rule it can only ever fire at `stock = 0`, which is exactly
where the P2.5 unconditional floor already fires. As a units rule it does the work nobody else does —
on a shelf with cover 0 and a dry warehouse it converts a line the engine would have passed over in
**silence** into a NAMED `blocked_no_wh` row. ⭐ **That is LAW 5, and it is the difference between a
pin that means something and a pin that decorates.**

⭐ **TWO LADDER ORDERINGS, BOTH LOAD-BEARING.** Availability outranks the pin (`blocked_no_wh` before
`pin_floor`) because **a pin raises DEMAND and never conjures STOCK**. The pin outranks the expiry
ceiling (`AND NOT pin_binds` on the expiry branch) because a binding pin already overrode the ceiling
inside the `GREATEST`, so naming the ceiling would name a constraint that decided nothing.

⛔ **THE BASE `jsonb_build_object` WAS AT 49 PAIRS = 98 ARGUMENTS, one pair from the 100-arg
ceiling.** A prior leg had already killed every engine run this exact way with `54023` and left the
warning in the source. The four pin keys went into a THIRD merged object. ⭐ **This migration is the
first change to test whether that warning would be read rather than scrolled past.**

⭐ **REGRESSION SAFETY IS STRUCTURAL, NOT TESTED-IN.** `pin_floor_units` is 0 on every unpinned line
⇒ `pin_binds` is FALSE (never NULL: `FALSE AND NULL` is `FALSE` in SQL, which is why the predicate is
ordered with the `> 0` test first) ⇒ the new branch never fires and the expiry branch keeps its
original condition. An unpinned fleet plans byte-identically.

### The falsification — one targeted red

⭐ Hoisting `pin_floor` above `blocked_no_wh` produced **exactly one red: seq 16,
`got=pin_floor exp=blocked_no_wh`.** Not a cascade — one, at precisely the assertion written for it.

⛔ **THE GUARD PRECEDES THE CONTRADICTION GUARD, AND THAT ORDERING IS THE WHOLE UNIT.** "Revoke the
live `always_stock` first" is **true but misleading**: it invites CS to retire a standing rule to
unblock an approval that would still fail afterwards. An unconditional refusal must outrank a
conditional one. ⭐ **Falsified, not argued** — hoisting it below produced exactly **3 reds
(35/41/44)**, and hoisting it above the reject branch produced exactly **1 red (43)**. Each
falsification reddened precisely the assertion written for it.

⛔ **REJECTION STAYS LEGAL, BY CONSTRUCTION.** The guard sits inside the approve branch, after the
reject branch returns. A proposal that could be neither approved nor rejected would sit in CS's queue
forever — trading a silent wrong answer for a permanent stuck one. New probe (l) proves it, run in a
rolled-back subtransaction so `pr3` stays `pending` for seq 36.

⭐ **THE NEW PROBE KEY DELIBERATELY DOES NOT START WITH `neg`.** seq 39 counts `key LIKE 'neg%'` and
expects exactly 11; a twelfth refusal probe would have reddened an anti-vacuity assertion with
nothing to do with this change. ⛔ **Read the anti-vacuity assertions before adding a probe.**

**Five status vocabularies, one definition.** `approved`+`applied` → accepted · `rejected` → rejected
· `pending`+`proposed` → undecided · `unclaimed` → unmatched (an offer that found no target was never
put to CS) · `superseded`+`expired` → **withdrawn**, the load-bearing distinction: counting a
superseded proposal as a rejection punishes the miner for CS's latency, counting it as an acceptance
overstates. Denominator is accepted+rejected only. An `unmapped` bucket and a published
`bucket_sum_ok` mean a status added by a future migration cannot silently move the rate.

⛔ **ZERO EVIDENCE IS NOT A FAILING GRADE.** `decided = 0` → `NULL` and `insufficient_evidence`, never
`0.00` / `fail`. G12's bar is "≥60% or the miner is noise"; rendering an unreviewed queue as 0% would
retire a working miner on no evidence at all.

**Cody caught a real bug at review.** Dara's helper draft ended `… >= p_bar_pct THEN 'pass' ELSE
'fail'`. `(100.0*a/d) >= NULL` is NULL, not TRUE, so **a missing threshold would have rendered as
`fail`** — S-126 in a new organ. Cody also refused `LIMIT 1` without `ORDER BY` on
`refill_policy_params`: one row by convention, not by structure (S-138's shape). Both fixed before
apply; seq 41 now pins the NULL-bar arm.

**S-140 (NEW) — the default-privileges trap is wider than leg 87 recorded.** The view landed
`authenticated=arwdDxtm` from a migration containing both `REVOKE ALL … FROM PUBLIC` and
`GRANT SELECT … TO authenticated`: the default grant is **per-role and explicit**, so revoking from
`PUBLIC` removed nothing and the GRANT added nothing already held. It applies to **views** and to
**`authenticated`**, not just functions and `anon`. Corrected forward. ⭐ And seq 49 pins the **whole
`relacl` string**, not "no anon" — a no-anon assertion would have passed straight over the
over-grant, which is S-132/S-139's shape again.

would have left `live_*` pinned at 0 and asserted **nothing** about the half of the object that
matters — S-132's vacuity in a new organ, on the very leg meant to be learning from it. So the
scenario plants at **1999-01-01**: unmistakably synthetic to any human, yet BELOW the epoch, so it
drives the live path for real. It reaches **pass** (feedback_pins, 4/5 = 80%), **fail**
(picker_weights, 1/5 = 20%, proving `applied` → accepted) and **insufficient_evidence** (rotation,
untouched) through the view, and asserts the partition in BOTH directions — the fixture side is

DECLARED `plan_date` to sit inside 2030, so 59 declares `2030-06-01` and never uses the
`{{plan_date}}` token; the constraint governs the declared date, not what the scenario plants.

## [2026-08-01 leg 90 · unit 2] P4.4 SPOT-BUY — DARA DESIGN + CODY REVIEW COMPLETE (nothing built)

**Task:** P4.4 `create_spot_purchase_v3` (fixture 18), the first owed item after P4.3 closed.

⭐ **FIRST, THE LEG-88 DUPLICATE CHECK, and it came back clean:** there is **no `%spot%` function
anywhere in `pg_proc`** and **no golden fixture** whose name or `source_incident` mentions spot-buy
or walk-in. P4.4 is genuinely unbuilt and **fixture id 18 is free** — it does not already exist
under another id (the 4→41 / 13→40 / 25→50 trap that cost legs 69-78).

⭐ **CS IS ALREADY DOING SPOT BUYS BY HAND — the live PO ledger names them:** `PO-2026-CF0731SPOT`
and `PO-2026-CF0731SPOT2` (po_number 9245 / 9248, Carrefour, both received). P4.4 is not a new
business act; it is making an existing manual one atomic. That reframes the RPC as a **parity**
target, which is why the design asserts PO-side column-by-column parity with the incumbent receiver.

**DELIVERED: `docs/prds/PRD-110-P4.4-DARA-spot-buy-design.md`** — signature, transaction order,
a 46-assertion fixture plan, Cody's verdict + 5 conditions. ⛔ **No migration applied, no dial
added, nothing half-built.**

**THE THREE LANDMINES — each read out of live code, none mentioned in the BUILD SPEC. These are the
value of this unit; the naive build hits all three:**

- ⛔ **L1 — `receive_purchase_order` HARDCODES `public.wh_central_id()`** (`v_warehouse_id` is set
  from it at DECLARE and used for both lines and additions; there is no warehouse argument). But
  `bind_dispatch_fefo` picks with `p.warehouse_id = COALESCE(rd.from_warehouse_id, wh_central_id())`.
  **So a spot buy for an MCC-served machine receives to CENTRAL, the binder looks in MCC, the line
  never binds — and `blocked_demand` would still get stamped `resolved='spot_buy'`.** A silent qty-0
  wearing a resolution (LAW 5). → **D-A: the v3 RPC does its own receive into a REQUIRED
  `p_warehouse_id` and does NOT call `receive_purchase_order`** (Article 3: add `_v3`, never mutate
  an incumbent the whole procurement FE depends on).
- ⛔ **L2 — `create_purchase_order` FORCES a driver task for every walk-in supplier:**
  `v_needs_task := (v_procurement_type = 'walk_in') OR (p_force_driver_task = true)`. Passing
  `p_force_driver_task => false` **cannot suppress it**, and every spot supplier is walk-in. The RPC
  would mint a `pending` task telling a driver to go buy goods **he is already holding.** →
  **D-B: still CALL the incumbent** (it owns `po_number_seq` drift self-healing, the PRD-1
  `boonz_product_block_reason` guardrail and `procurement_events`) **then auto-CLOSE the task in the
  same transaction** with an event. ⛔ Never DELETE the task row.
- ⛔ **L3 — `bind_dispatch_fefo` is machine-scoped by `official_name[]`, and passing NULL sweeps the
  FLEET.** One driver's Carrefour run must not bind other machines' lines to his batch. → **D-C:
  always call it with the single machine's name**, and **surface `still_unbound_no_wh_stock` in the
  return jsonb rather than swallowing it** — a spot buy of the wrong item binds nothing and the
  caller has to be told.

**VERIFIED LIVE THIS LEG (claims the design rests on, probed not assumed):**

- ✅ `inventory_events.kind` CHECK **does** admit `spot_buy_receive` — and it carries a **SIGN**
  constraint: `qty_delta > 0` is forced for `load|venue_fill|spot_buy_receive`, `< 0` for the
  consuming kinds, plus a global `qty_delta <> 0`. ⚠️ **Only `correction` and `derived_decrement`
  have ever been written** — `spot_buy_receive` is an unexercised path and fixture 18 is its first.
- ✅ `blocked_demand` = **52 rows, ALL OPEN**, and **no row has ever been resolved by anything**.
  P4.4 writes the first `resolved_at` in the table's life; `blocked_demand_resolution_pair` forces
  `resolved_at`+`resolution` together. ⏸️ **Cody's recorded condition:** any blocked-aging/burn-down
  metric is therefore **unexercised** — do not report "blocked demand is being worked" off the first
  week of spot data. That is precisely the leg-88 G12 lesson repeating in a new table.
- ✅ `refill_policy_params` is **81 columns**, not the pointer's 78 — leg 89's three miner dials
  account for exactly the difference (78+3). Pointer arithmetic reconciled, not contradicted.
- ✅ Walk-in suppliers Active: Carrefour `a44b3e6c-...` (**the supplier in the 07-30 01:21
  incident**), Union Coop `31b6355d`, Arab Sweet, Jaleel, Merich, Annachamb. ⛔ DUP `3cec0b3a` is
  Inactive — never target it.

⭐ **DESIGN CALL D-D — the pre-auth cap ships ENFORCED-AS-`warn`, not parked as a no-op.** BUILD SPEC
said "park the param". Building it dark would make an invisible cap indistinguishable from no cap,
so the design adds `spot_buy_price_cap_aed` (default **15**) + `spot_buy_cap_enforcement` default
**`'warn'`**, mirroring `preflight_enforcement`'s house pattern. **The parked DECISIONS-READY item
becomes the flip to `'block'`, not the cap's existence.** Every breach is visible from day one at
zero ops risk.

| ---------------- | ------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------- |

`n_fail=0`, `n_expected_red=0`, no `scenario_error`, not vacuous, on **two consecutive committed
runs** per S-136. Golden **49 -> 50 fixtures**, **1655 -> 1735 assertions**.

⭐ **THE FIXTURE EXERCISES THE REAL WRITE PATH (`p_dry_run=false`) ACROSS FOUR PROTECTED TABLES AND
LEAVES ZERO ROWS.** Plant + 12 refusal probes + a dry run + the committed write all run inside ONE
plpgsql subtransaction that ends with `RAISE EXCEPTION 'FX18_ROLLBACK'`. Rows roll back; plpgsql
**variables survive**, so every value the assertions need is captured into `s_*` before the unwind
and written to `golden.scratch` after it. This is the same mechanism the RPC uses for its own dry run.

⛔ **S-153 - THE REASON IT HAD TO BE BUILT THAT WAY, AND IT IS NOT A STYLE CHOICE.** The first draft
reclaimed by DELETE and hit
`inventory_audit_log_wh_inventory_id_fkey`: `warehouse_inventory` is FK-referenced by the
**append-only** audit log, so deleting a received batch requires erasing audit rows, which Article 7
forbids. **A fixture cannot delete-reclaim a warehouse receive.** Rolling back never writes them.
⚠️ The one thing rollback cannot undo is `nextval('po_number_seq')` - sequences are non-transactional,
so each run burns one `po_number`. Recorded now rather than discovered as a mystery gap later; same
accepted class as fixture 60's permanent `miner_runs_v3` rows.

⛔ **S-154 - THE SAFETY PROPERTY HIDING IN THE CALLER'S ROLE.** Fixture 18 calls as a **`warehouse`**
user, not `operator_admin`, and that is deliberate. Per S-145 the owner-only attach path sends the
RPC at _today's open walk-in PO for that supplier_ and then stamps `received_date` on its lines - so
an `operator_admin` fixture would, on any day procurement has an open Carrefour PO, **receive a real
production purchase order**. Leg 91's dry run returned `po_path:minted` only because no such PO
existed that minute. That was luck. For a `warehouse` caller the attach path is unreachable and
`minted` is deterministic; **seq 12 pins it.**

⭐ **THREE MORE LANDMINES, ALL FOUND BY BUILDING (S-150/151/152):** `uq_blocked_demand_open` is keyed
at **SHELF** grain and `boonz_product_id` is not in the key, so two open blocks on one machine need
two shelves · `refill_dispatching.source_kind='wh'` **requires** `source_warehouse_id`, and
`'warehouse'` is not a legal `source_kind` at all (it is a `source_origin` value) ·
`enforce_canonical_dispatch_write` **LOGS rather than blocks**, so a raw harness plant silently mints
`bypass_violation_log` rows - residue in a governance table where the fixture reads as an attacker.

written, and all three surfaced there in about a minute each.

### ⛔ S-155 - THE PIN IS SAFE _BECAUSE_ `run_fixture` CATCHES; AN INNER HANDLER WOULD BREAK IT

This was the one thing that could have gone wrong. Pinning mutates `weimi_device_status`, a LIVE
observation. `golden.run_fixture` runs `scenario_sql` inside `BEGIN ... EXCEPTION WHEN OTHERS` - a

correct, and ⛔ **adding a handler to "harden" it would be strictly worse**: execution would continue
past a failed restore and leave the live observation modified. ⭐ **Generalise: before wrapping a
harness block in an exception handler, check whether the CALLER's handler is what makes it safe.**

### ⛔ S-158 - THE PARKED PREMISE WAS FALSE, AND PROBING FIRST IS WHAT CAUGHT IT

D-36 said `write_audit_log` "records two ordinary edits and no swap". **It records nothing.**
`plan_edits_v3` carries no `audit_log_write` trigger at all - only `tg_plan_edits_v3_append_only`
and `_no_truncate` - and `write_audit_log` holds **zero** rows for `swap_v3`,
`record_plan_edit_v3` or `plan_edits_v3`. Built to the parked wording, the fix would have aimed at
an audit trail that does not exist.

⭐ **The real defect is narrower and worse.** `set_config(..., true)` is **TRANSACTION-scoped**, not
statement-scoped: `swap_v3` RETURNED leaving `record_plan_edit_v3` behind, so the next write to any
of the **42** audited tables in that transaction was stamped with the inner writer rather than the
act the human performed. **Measured live before a line was written:** after a successful swap,
`current_setting('app.rpc_name')` = `record_plan_edit_v3`. ⛔ **A parking-lot entry records what a
leg BELIEVED. Probe the mechanism live before executing the fix** - PRD-106's stale-root-cause
lesson, recurring at decision grain.

### ⭐ S-159 - `swap_v3` WAS THE LONE OUTLIER; THE CONVENTION WAS ALREADY LOAD-BEARING

Fleet probe: every other v3 writer that calls an inner `rpc_name`-setter already re-asserts -
`create_spot_purchase_v3` (3), `mine_edit_history_v3` (3), `run_weekly_miners_v3` (2),
`submit_feedback_v3` (2) - and fixtures **56/57/58** already pin `rpc_name_after_<call>` for three of
them. So D-36 was not inventing a convention, it was closing the one gap in an existing one, and the
assertion idiom was already chosen. ⏸️ **S-160 PARKED:** `stitch_v3`, `run_pipeline_v3` (four inner
setters), `run_nightly_shadow_v3`, `driver_confirm_shelf_v3`, `estimate_shelf_composition_v3`,
`record_inventory_event_v3` carry the same leak. **D-36 names `swap_v3` only; LAW 10 says do not
drift.** A fleet sweep is its own unit.

### ⭐ THE ANCHOR SPREAD (S-157 APPLIED), SMOKE-PROBED AND ROLLED BACK FIRST

Probe run before any assertion existed, then discarded by `RAISE`: successful two-leg swap →
`record_plan_edit_v3` · refused swap → the caller's own sentinel **survives**, because the caught
raise rolls that subtransaction back · `app.via_rpc` → `true` throughout. ⭐ **The refused anchor is
GREEN before AND after the fix - that is precisely what proves seq 62 measures the inner calls
rather than the probe.** A fix that did nothing could not produce this spread.

### ⛔ S-161 - HERMETICITY WAS AN OBLIGATION HERE, NOT A NICETY

`golden.run_all()` runs every fixture in ONE transaction, and a subtransaction that **COMMITS** does
not roll `set_config` back (contrast S-155, which concerns one that ABORTS). Fixture **60 seq 54
reads the ambient `app.rpc_name` without setting it first**, so a sentinel left behind here would
have reddened fixture 60 for a reason unrelated to fixture 60 - the same cross-boundary leak class
D-36 is about, reappearing inside the harness. Step 6 therefore captures on entry and restores on
exit, and seq 67 asserts it. **Proven by running 54 then 60 in one shared transaction: `f54_fail=0`,
`f60_fail=0`, value between them `compose_plan_with_edits_v3`** - what fixture 60 would have seen
anyway, not the sentinel.

### ⭐ THE PREMISE WAS EXACT THIS TIME, AND PROBING IT STILL EARNED ITS KEEP

S-158 made re-derivation mandatory after D-36's parked wording turned out to be false. Here the
wording held exactly: the helper exists as described, `run_nightly_shadow_v3` asks it by name, and
`_build_draft_core_v3` did not and still carried the bare `EXTRACT(DOW FROM p_plan_date) = 6`.
⭐ **It is the probe that is the rule, not the outcome** - and the probe run _around_ the premise is
what found the two things below, neither of which is in D-35, the BUILD SPEC, or the design.

### ⛔ S-164 - A SYNTHETIC 2030 DATE IS NOT AUTOMATICALLY AN EMPTY ONE

LAW 12 says test on synthetic 2030 plan_dates. It does **not** say a 2030 date is unoccupied, and
this build has been colonising them for 95 legs. `_build_draft_core_v3` exits early on a Saturday, on
a live plan, and on zero included machines - but on a date carrying **confirmed + included**
`machines_to_visit` rows it walks into `engine_add_pod` / `engine_swap_pod` / `engine_finalize_pod`
under its own pinned `statement_timeout` of **20 minutes**.

⛔ **`2030-03-05..2030-03-14` carry EIGHT `machines_to_visit` rows each** (fixture 58's cast). The
first window this leg chose was inside that range and the fixture's own virginity guard refused it -
**the guard caught it before the engines ran, which is the only reason this is a lesson and not an
incident.** ⭐ Probe the window before calling anything that plans, and make the fixture **re-probe
on every run**: seq 3 turns a colonised window into a red instead of a runaway. `2030-06-03..09` was
verified virgin on four tables before the file existed.

### ⛔ S-165 - A HELPER WITH A LARGER GUARD SET IS NOT A DROP-IN FOR AN INLINE RULE

`is_refill_planning_day_v3(p)` = `p IS NOT NULL AND EXTRACT(DOW FROM p) <> 6`; the inline rule was
`EXTRACT(DOW FROM p) = 6`. **They differ on NULL** - the inline rule declines the branch, `NOT
helper(NULL)` takes it, so a naive swap converts a raise into a silent `skipped_saturday`. Safe at
this site only because `IF p_plan_date IS NULL THEN RAISE` runs three lines above. The migration
asserts that ordering **positionally on the live body** and REFUSES rather than assuming it.
⭐ **Generalise: before collapsing an inline rule onto a named helper, diff the GUARD SETS, not the
happy paths.** Article 16 convergence is exactly where this class of bug lives, and D-27/D-28/D-31
are all convergence units.

### ⭐ THE SPREAD IS WHAT MAKES THE AGREEMENT MEAN ANYTHING (S-157 APPLIED)

The fixture does not assert "the helper exists". It calls Stage 1 on **seven consecutive days** and
compares "did it take the Saturday exit?" against the helper's verdict. Seq 7 requires **zero
disagreements** - but a helper stuck at TRUE and a Stage 1 that never skips would satisfy that
perfectly, so seq 8/9/10 require **exactly one** skip, on the Saturday, with the helper independently
rejecting exactly one day whose DOW is **6**. ⭐ **Seq 7/8/9/10 are green BEFORE and AFTER the
collapse by design** - that is the LAW 12 proof that a refactor refactored, and seq 4/5 are the two
that carry the red.

### ⭐ THE PREMISE HELD, AND PROBING AROUND IT IS STILL WHAT PAID

S-158 makes re-derivation mandatory. S-130's claim held exactly - `record_plan_edit_v3` genuinely did
not mention `planning_pins_v3` or the pins view anywhere, so the edit really did win in silence. ⭐ But
the probes run _around_ the premise produced the three findings below, none of which is in D-38, the
BUILD SPEC, or any design doc. **It is the probe that is the rule, not the outcome.**

### ⛔ THE DESIGN DECISION THAT MATTERS: THE EDIT PATH ASKS THE ENGINE, IT DOES NOT RECOMPUTE

`engine_add_pod_v3` already writes `pin_floor_units` / `pin_count` / `pin_binds` / `need_raw_no_pin`
onto **every** shadow line (0 explicitly when unpinned, LAW 5), and `record_plan_edit_v3` already
resolves that exact base row to compute `base_qty_at_edit`. So the floor is a **read**, not a
derivation. ⛔ Recomputing it from `v_planning_pins_active_v3` would have put a second copy of the pin
ladder in a second function - the Article 16 sin D-35 retired **one migration earlier**, with S-165's
guard-set trap attached. ⭐ Two further calls that are not obvious and are now pinned:
**(i) the FLOOR is the test, not `pin_binds`** - a floor of 6 on a line the ladder took to 9 does not
bind, yet an edit to 3 is still an override; gating on `pin_binds` misses that whole class.
**(ii) the edit must have LOWERED it** - `floor > 0 AND effective < floor AND effective < base`. The
third clause stops a line the ENGINE left short being blamed on the next human, and stops an `add`
raising a short line TOWARD its floor being logged as an override of that very pin.

### **CODY: ⚠️ APPROVE WITH REVISIONS - three, all real, all applied BEFORE apply**

- **⛔ R1 (silent-zero)** `pin_contradiction NOT NULL DEFAULT false` would backfill every pre-D-38 row
  to "false", claiming _evaluated, no contradiction_ about edits never checked against a pin. Made
  NULLABLE. ⭐ **Confirmed live after apply: 182 of 196 rows read NULL** - under the original design
  all 182 would be lying, and every future G12 read would inherit it (S-168).
- **⛔ R2 (impossible declaration)** the FK was `ON DELETE SET NULL`, which is an UPDATE against an
  append-only table: the trigger raises and the delete fails anyway. Changed to `RESTRICT`, which
  states the true intent and matches every other FK on the ledger.
- **⛔ R3 (Article 16 documentation)** METRICS_REGISTRY now records that the edit path consumes
  **engine-recorded provenance**, not the pins view, so a later leg cannot "converge" it and silently
  reintroduce the duplication.

### ⛔ THE APPEND-ONLY TRIGGER HAD TO LEARN THE NEW COLUMNS, OR "LOUDLY" DECAYS TO "SILENTLY"

Found by reading the trigger rather than trusting the table's reputation: `tg_plan_edits_v3_append_only`
enumerates its immutable columns as an **explicit tuple**. A column it does not name is silently
UPDATE-able, so without PART 3 the pin-contradiction record could be erased after the fact - the
evidence D-38 exists to create would have been the one part of the row anyone could quietly edit.
Fixture 62 seq 5 pins it.

## [2026-08-03 leg 97 · unit 1] **S-166 CLOSED - GOLDEN IS FULLY GREEN AGAIN, AND THE RED WAS BIGGER THAN REPORTED**

| version          | name                                                         | result                                       |
| ---------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ | -------------------------------------------- |
| `20260803192110` | `prd110_p3_s166_gate0_queue_delta_not_constant`              | 3 bodies + 3 assertions · **11/50/51 GREEN** |
| `20260803192227` | `prd110_p3_s166_gate0_queue_delta_not_constant_reapply_noop` | same body twice = idempotency proof, no-op   |

### ⛔ THE HEADLINE: LEG 96 REPORTED TWO REDS. THERE WERE THREE.

Fixture **11 seq 38** carries the identical pinned-`1240` shape as 50 seq 46 and 51 seq 51. It read
**GREEN** at pickup - because it had not run since **2026-08-01**, so its `golden.scratch` row still
held the pre-drift 1240 and the assertion was comparing a stale capture to a stale constant. Running
it at this leg's RED baseline turned it red immediately: **`actual 1330`**. ⭐ **A green status on a
fixture that has not run since before the drift is a CACHED result, not a verified one** (S-169). The
pointer's instruction to "audit other fixtures for the same shape" is what surfaced it; taking
last-known run results at face value would have left a live red in the harness.

### THE FIX IS THE SHAPE, NOT THE NUMBER

Each body now captures `machines_to_visit` **BEFORE** the scenario runs (`golden.scratch` key
`tripwires_before`, inserted immediately after the body's own `DELETE FROM golden.scratch`, the
earliest possible point); the existing tripwire section already captured it AFTER; the assertion
subtracts and expects `0`. ⛔ **Bumping 1240 -> 1330 was refused** - it re-arms the identical decay
and yields an assertion that is green and meaningless.

⛔ **The obvious shortcut was rejected on inspection.** Fixture 11 seq 39 already solves drift for
`pod_refills` by re-counting live at assertion time, and copying it would have needed **no body edit
at all**. It is drift-immune but **weak**: both readings happen AFTER the body, so a body that wrote
rows would have them in both and the delta would still read 0. Only a BEFORE-vs-AFTER pair can fail
for the reason the tripwire exists (S-170).

### **CODY: ⚠️ APPROVE WITH REVISIONS - one, real, applied BEFORE apply**

- **⛔ R1 (atomicity)** the draft was **two** `DO` blocks = two statements. A failure in the second
  leaves bodies carrying a before-capture that no assertion reads - a half-applied migration, exactly
  what the RELAY handoff invariant forbids. Collapsed into ONE `DO` block so atomicity does not depend
  on the runner's transaction semantics rather than being assumed from them.
- Class **(f) non-protected** - `golden` is test infrastructure. ⭐ **Article 16 checked and does not
  bind:** `machines_to_visit` IS the base table of `v_pick_decision_cohorts_v3`, but a raw `count(*)`
  used as a write-tripwire is not a re-derivation of the cohort metric.

### ⭐ NON-VACUITY PROVEN, NOT ASSUMED

A green assertion that cannot go red is the S-132 trap. Proven by perturbing `golden.scratch` inside a
`DO` block that **raises to roll itself back**, so the proof left nothing behind:
**board moves by 7 -> `7`** · **before-capture never ran -> `absent`**. Both red. The
`COALESCE(...,'absent')` is what stops a missing capture passing as NULL.

### VERIFIED AFTER APPLY, BY DIRECT QUERY

RED baseline captured on all three first (`1330` vs `1240`). After: **11 (39/0) · 50 (49/0) ·
51 (53/0)**, green on **two consecutive full runs**. `golden.fixtures` **52** and `golden.assertions`
**1792** both UNCHANGED (3 rewritten, 0 added). Zero `expect='1240'` survivors. Re-apply verified a
true no-op (marker still once per body, 3 assertions still deltas, 1792 unchanged).
**0 flags flipped · 0 cron schedules changed · 0 engine functions touched.**

### ⛔ S-171 RAISED BY THE PROOF ITSELF

Proving idempotency by RE-APPLYING as a migration worked - and minted a second `schema_migrations`
row with no disk file, i.e. exactly the DB∖disk gap every STEP R checks for. **Filed at
`20260803192227` in the same unit** rather than carried. Later legs: prove idempotency via
`/tmp/prd110_sql.sh`, which mints no row.

### ⏸️ THE DECAYING-ABSOLUTE SWEEP IS COMPLETE (S-166 follow-through)

All enabled assertions with `eq`/`gte`/`lte` on a 3+ digit constant and no 2030 scoping were swept.
**Only three are `eq`:** `f37 seq14` = `23514` (a **SQLSTATE**, not a count) · `f42 seq9` = `480` (a
**param default**) · `f37 seq24` = `141` (`engine_forecast_error_v3` on `2026-06-26 AND
actuals_settled`) - **the one true cousin, re-derived live at this leg and still exactly 141, green**.
Left deliberately: a PAST fully-settled date is not a nightly-growing queue. Everything else is `gte`,
a floor on a population that only grows, drift-tolerant by construction.

### THE UNIT: D-19 — and why the answer was "not yet"

The leg-97 pointer's warning was exact and it paid. D-19 reads like `UPDATE refill_policy_params SET
preflight_enforcement='block';`. It is not.

**Step 1 — the premise held.** `preflight_override_v3(date,text)` exists, is role-gated, refuses a
reason under 10 characters, refuses to grant when preflight does NOT fail (no banking a blanket grant),
does not stack, and is genuinely **single-use**: `commit_refill_plan` writes
`refill_commit_log.preflight_override_id`, and the unspent-grant lookup is `NOT EXISTS` against exactly
that column. ⭐ **Fixture 33 re-run live at this leg per S-169: GREEN 35/35.** Not trusted — re-derived.

**Step 2 — the premise was also incomplete, and that is the finding.** `preflight_enforcement` is one
global flag arming **three** paths. Fixture 33 covers one of them, and
`grep -rn commit_refill_plan src/` proves it is **the one with no FE caller at all**.

| path                        | gated            | hatch                                         | FE caller                       |
| --------------------------- | ---------------- | --------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------- |
| `commit_refill_plan`        | yes              | `preflight_override_v3`, audited + single-use | **none**                        |
| `stitch_pod_to_boonz`       | yes              | inline `p_force` + ≥10-char reason            | `RefillPlanningTab.tsx:680`     |
| `commit_refill_plan_atomic` | **transitively** | **none**                                      | `:960` — the only commit button |

`commit_refill_plan_atomic` calls `stitch_pod_to_boonz(p_plan_date, false)` then RAISEs unless
`v_stitch->'write_result'->>'status'='ok'`. A block-mode refusal carries **no `write_result` key**, so
the operator receives `commit_refill_plan_atomic: stitch write_result=null — rolling back (PRD-019 E2).`

⭐ **The teeth are real** — the commit rolls back, zero `refill_plan_output` rows (fixture 63 seq 50/51).
⛔ **The recovery is not** — the invariant id, the `fix_path` and the `p_force` instructions are all
discarded before the operator sees them, and the function hard-codes `false` with no `p_force`
passthrough. **Flipping today arms a guard and removes its escape hatch in one statement**, at the site
nobody had checked. ⚠️ Worse, it would be **inert until it wasn't**: live preflight is `PASS` / **0
violations** for both `CURRENT_DATE` and `resolve_refill_plan_date()` = `2026-08-04`, so the flip bites
only at the first real violation — exactly when CS would be stranded. Full analysis + the two-step
unblock: **S-172** in the PARKING-LOT.

### ⭐ THE REUSABLE TRICK IN FIXTURE 63 — and the price it charges

Parents are seeded `status='stitched'`, never `'approved'`, so `stitch_pod_to_boonz` always halts at its
own `no approved rows` guard, which sits **after** the preflight gate. **"Reached `no approved rows`" is
a safe, deterministic marker for "the gate let this through"** — and no call in the fixture can ever run
a real stitch, which is what makes probing a live production commit path safe at all.
⚠️ **The price:** the `p_force` path's `preflight_override_log` INSERT is rolled back by that same halt,
so `override_log_delta` is **0 on every probe by construction**. Asserting it as a delta would be
vacuous (S-132's disease), so seq 43 asserts the audited-write shape on the **column default** instead.

### ⛔ TWO DEFECTS I SHIPPED, AND NEITHER WAS FOUND BY READING THE CODE

**1. The CHECK that accepted the one row it existed to forbid.** `ck_scoreboard_engine_tag` read
`(metric_key='wmape' AND engine_tag IN ('v3','v19')) OR (metric_key<>'wmape' AND engine_tag IS NULL)`.
For an untagged `wmape` row that is `(TRUE AND NULL) OR FALSE` = **NULL** — and **a CHECK constraint
accepts a NULL result.** It read correctly to Dara and to Cody. **Only fixture 65 seq 10, which
actually attempted the forbidden INSERT, found it.** Rewritten as a `CASE` (always TRUE/FALSE).
⭐ **S-177: never validate a constraint by reading its predicate; write the adversarial INSERT.**

**2. A metric that could never once be produced.** `composition_confidence_avg` was gated on
`p_metric_date = today Dubai`, while the only caller that ever runs it (cron 47) computes
Dubai-**yesterday**. The branch was **unreachable by construction** — the metric would have read
vacuous forever while looking perfectly healthy. Caught by the vacuity map on the first backfill
(14/14 vacuous), not by review. Window widened to `[today-1, today]`; anything older still refuses
rather than back-stamping today's confidence onto last week. ⭐ **This is exactly S-173/S-174: a value
that can never be reached is the same defect as a green that can never go red.** Seq 23 is the
permanent tripwire.

**3. And a third, from read-back rather than review (S-140).** Supabase's `ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES`
grants every new `public` table to `anon` **and** `authenticated` at CREATE. The explicit
`REVOKE ... FROM anon` worked; `GRANT SELECT TO authenticated` did **not** reduce the `arwdDxtm` it
already held — only RLS stood between `authenticated` and INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE. Now
`{postgres=arwdDxtm/postgres,service_role=arwdDxtm/postgres,authenticated=r/postgres}`, pinned whole
by seq 20. ⭐ **S-178.**

⭐ **The fixture carries real positive controls, not just red-when-broken checks.** Seq 8 proves the
vacuity CHECK still ACCEPTS a legitimate vacuous row (without it, seq 6 and 7 would both pass if the
constraint simply refused everything). Seq 12 seeds one real `expired_sold_incident` and proves the
counter moves **0 → 1** — a count-of-a-bad-thing that sits at 0 forever is indistinguishable from a
detector that cannot see. That control runs inside a deliberately rolled-back subtransaction:
`inventory_events` (cron 44's table) measured **50 before and 50 after**.
